traits.description: Mimics the voice of the person it replaced or of anyone whose personality it consumed; a DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check reveals the imitation.

traits.name: Sorrowful Memento
traits.description: Disadvantage on D20 Tests while it can see a creature holding a possession of the person it replaced.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: One Claw and one Pitchfork attack, and Personality Consumption if available.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 5 ft.; 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic.

actions.name: Pitchfork
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 10 ft.; 7 (1d8 + 3) Piercing, and it can push or pull a Medium or smaller target 5 feet.

actions.name: Personality Consumption (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Intelligence save DC 12, one creature it can see within 30 feet: Stunned until the end of its next turn and Intelligence reduced by 1d4, dying at 0. A Humanoid slain this way is replaced by a new Pumpkin Head 1d8 hours later unless its body is burned.

traits.name: Undead Fortitude
traits.description: If damage other than Radiant or a Critical Hit reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it makes a Constitution save (DC 5 + the damage), dropping to 1 Hit Point instead on a success.

actions.name: Beak
actions.description: Melee attack, +4, reach 5 ft.; 4 (1d4 + 2) Piercing plus 3 (1d6) Necrotic.

actions.name: Harbinger of Doom (2/Day)
actions.description: Wisdom save DC 11, one creature within 60 feet: 5 (1d10) Psychic and Frightened until the end of its next turn, half damage only on success.

reactions.name: Death Veil
reactions.description: A creature within 30 feet making a Death Saving Throw has Advantage on it.

display.senses: blindsight 10 ft. (Drone only), darkvision 60 ft.; passive Perception 14

traits.name: Compelled Contest
traits.description: It can't refuse a musical contest: a creature can make a Charisma (Performance) check with a Musical Instrument as an Influence action, and the reveler must succeed on a Charisma save against that total or take 20 Psychic and be Stunned until the end of the creature's next turn.

traits.name: Dancing Step
traits.description: Doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks when it leaves an enemy's reach.

traits.name: Ensemble Form
traits.description: It takes the Drone (hurdy-gurdy), Drum (frame drum), or Bell (handbells) form, which sets some traits and actions.

traits.name: Droning Swarm (Drone Only)
traits.description: Bees surround it; a creature that ends its turn in its 10-foot Emanation makes a DC 16 Constitution save or is Poisoned until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Instrumental Blast attacks.

actions.name: Instrumental Blast
actions.description: Melee or ranged attack, +8, reach 5 ft. or range 90 ft.; 14 (2d8 + 5) Thunder.

actions.name: Infectious Rhythm (Drum Only)
actions.description: Wisdom save DC 16, up to two creatures it can see within 30 feet: 18 (4d8) Psychic and affected by Irresistible Dance (no Concentration needed), half damage only on success.

actions.name: Stunning Clangor (Bell Only)
actions.description: Constitution save DC 16, one creature it can see within 60 feet: 40 (9d8) Thunder and Stunned until the end of the reveler's next turn, half damage only on success.

display.senses: darkvision 60 ft., truesight 120 ft. (Witch only); passive Perception 16

traits.name: Moral Quandary
traits.description: A creature can use a Bonus Action to recite a story's moral matching its form, weakening it for 1 hour: no Reactions and AC reduced by 4.

traits.name: Storied Form
traits.description: It takes the Great Beast, Hero, or Witch form (monsters, heroes, or wicked magicians), which sets some traits and Fabled Assault. In Hero form its AC is 17.

traits.name: Terror Feeding (Witch Only)
traits.description: If a Frightened creature is within 30 feet at the end of its turn, it gains 15 Temporary Hit Points.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Three Thrash attacks; it can replace one with Fabled Assault if available.

actions.name: Thrash
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 10 ft.; 18 (3d8 + 5) Force.

actions.name: Fabled Assault (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: By form: Consuming Bite (Great Beast; DC 17 Constitution save, one creature within 5 feet, Disadvantage if grappled by it: 36 (8d8) Necrotic, and a Huge or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 15) and Restrained while grappled, half damage only on success; it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage); Heroic Charge (Hero; moves its Speed in a line through creatures without provoking Opportunity Attacks, each creature whose space it enters making a DC 17 Strength save: 26 (4d12) Force and Prone, half damage only on success); Wicked Storm (Witch; DC 17 Dexterity save, 60-foot Cone: 27 (6d8) Lightning and Frightened with Speed 0, repeating the save each turn end and succeeding automatically after 1 minute; half damage only on success).

reactions.name: Dramatic Reversal
reactions.description: When hit by an attack roll, it adds 4 to its AC against that attack, possibly causing a miss.

traits.name: Fungal Step
traits.description: Ignores Difficult Terrain caused by plants or fungi.

traits.name: Hunting Horn
traits.description: It carries a horn with AC 16, 10 Hit Points, and immunity to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic.

traits.name: Iron Binding
traits.description: With iron wrapped around part of its body (bracelet, Manacles, or Chain, treated as Manacles), it can only do two of move, action, and Bonus Action each turn.

actions.name: Staff
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 5 ft.; 7 (1d8 + 3) Necrotic.

actions.name: Call the Rot (Requires Hunting Horn; Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Constitution save DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone: 11 (2d10) Necrotic and Poisoned until the end of its next turn, half damage only on success. The call carries 300 feet, and noncreature plants in the Cone rot and die.

display.speed: 5 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover; Orb of Water only), swim 30 ft.
display.languages: understands all languages but can't speak, telepathy 60 ft.

traits.name: Orb of Water
traits.description: A sphere of flowing water surrounds and moves with it, granting Fire Resistance while it is inside. A creature grappling it can pull it out; the orb then moves up to 20 feet toward it at the start of each of its turns, ending the grapple when it reaches the salmon.

traits.name: Water Breathing
traits.description: Can breathe only underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Water Spray attacks; it can replace one with Prophetic Guidance.

actions.name: Water Spray
actions.description: Ranged attack, +5, range 20/60 ft.; 6 (1d6 + 3) Cold.

actions.name: Prophetic Guidance (2/Day)
actions.description: A creature it can see within 30 feet can, once in the next minute, add 1d4 to a failed D20 Test, possibly turning it into a success.

reactions.name: Echo from the Current
reactions.description: When a creature within 5 feet makes an Intelligence or Wisdom check, it can use the salmon's Wisdom modifier (+4) instead of its own.

display.damageResistances: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
display.conditionImmunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained

traits.name: Mist Form
traits.description: Can enter and stop in another creature's space and move through a 1-inch gap at no extra cost.

traits.name: Corrupting Mist
traits.description: A creature that starts its turn in its space makes a DC 13 Constitution save, taking 10 (3d6) Necrotic or half on success. A Humanoid killed this way becomes a new shrouded at the start of the shrouded's next turn, acting on that Initiative, and can't be revived until the new one is destroyed.

traits.name: Graveyard Warding
traits.description: Can't pass a barrier or line of iron, such as a wrought-iron fence or iron filings; the barrier extends 1 mile up.

traits.name: Variation
traits.description: It is a Devourer, Reaper, or Whisperer, granting one unique action.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two melee attacks.

actions.name: Corrupting Touch
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 5 ft.; 6 (1d6 + 3) Necrotic.

actions.name: Consuming Bite (Devourer Only)
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 10 ft.; 5 (1d4 + 3) Bludgeoning, and a Medium or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 13), taking 10 (3d6) Necrotic at the start of each of its turns while grappled, which the shrouded regains as Hit Points.

actions.name: Scythe (Reaper Only)
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 5 ft.; 6 (1d6 + 3) Slashing plus 10 (3d6) Necrotic, and a creature can't regain Hit Points until the start of the shrouded's next turn.

actions.name: Toxic Thoughts (Whisperer Only)
actions.description: Intelligence save DC 13, each non-Construct, non-Undead creature in a 30-foot Emanation: 7 (2d6) Psychic and Frightened until the start of the shrouded's next turn, half damage only on success.

display.conditionImmunities: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious

traits.name: Corpse Fuel
traits.description: If it sees a corpse at the start of its turn, it must move into the corpse's space and use its action to burn it; Medium or smaller corpses become ash, larger ones shrink one size.

traits.name: Fire Form
traits.description: Moves through a 1-inch gap at no extra cost and can enter and stop in a creature's space, dealing 4 (1d8) Fire the first time it enters a creature's space on a turn.

traits.name: Illumination
traits.description: Sheds Dim Light in a 30-foot radius.

traits.name: Soul Burn
traits.description: At the end of each of its turns, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation takes 4 (1d8) Necrotic.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Sear attacks.

actions.name: Sear
actions.description: Melee attack, +5, reach 5 ft.; 7 (1d8 + 3) Fire, and the target has Disadvantage on its next attack before the stoker's next turn.

bonusActions.name: Spectral Steam (Recharge 5-6)
bonusActions.description: Dexterity save DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone: on failure it sheds Dim Light in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from being Invisible.

display.languages: understands Common and Sylvan but can't speak
display.conditionImmunities: charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, stunned

traits.name: Compelled Delivery
traits.description: As an Influence action, a creature can hand it a letter or parcel for a recipient the creature knows; the swarm is Charmed until it delivers it or takes damage, and must deliver it if it knows where the recipient is.

traits.name: Swarm
traits.description: Can share another creature's space and move through openings large enough for a Tiny pigeon; it can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.

traits.name: Unerring Delivery
traits.description: While delivering, it knows the distance and direction to the recipient on the same plane.

actions.name: Peck
actions.description: Melee attack, +4, reach 5 ft.; 5 (2d4) Piercing, or 2 (1d4) while Bloodied; while not Bloodied, a creature it hits is Charmed until the start of the swarm's next turn.

reactions.name: Many Eyes, One Voice (1/Day)
reactions.description: When a creature that gave it a delivery and is on the same plane uses an action to look through it, the swarm becomes a scrying sensor as if that creature cast Scrying, and the creature can speak through it.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If he fails a save, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Marshall Undead
traits.description: Undead of his choice (not himself) in his 60-foot Emanation have Advantage on attacks and saves, unless he is Incapacitated.

traits.name: Name of Rest
traits.description: His AC is 10 against attacks with a weapon inscribed with the runes of his original name, and he has Disadvantage on attacks against a creature holding one.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Three Soul Blade attacks; he can replace one with Life Drain.

actions.name: Soul Blade
actions.description: Melee or ranged attack, +14, reach 5 ft. or range 40/80 ft.; 17 (3d6 + 7) Slashing plus 13 (3d8) Necrotic, and a thrown blade returns to his hand.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.description: Constitution save DC 22, one creature within 5 feet: 16 (2d8 + 7) Necrotic and its Hit Point maximum drops by that much on failure. A Humanoid slain this way rises 24 hours later as a Wight under his control unless revived or its body is destroyed.

actions.name: Blade Storm (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 22, each creature of his choice in a 20-foot Emanation: 35 (10d6) Force and Prone, half damage only on success.

bonusActions.name: Undying Mount (Recharge 5-6)
bonusActions.description: Casts Phantom Steed without components, using Charisma; the steed takes no damage from area effects, and recasting ends the old one.

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: When hit while holding a weapon or shield, he adds 7 to his AC against that attack, possibly causing a miss.

legendaryActions.name: Death Grasp
legendaryActions.description: Strength save DC 22, one creature he can see within 100 feet: pulled up to 40 feet toward him by a ghostly arm and Speed halved until the end of its next turn, on failure.

legendaryActions.name: Grim Charge
legendaryActions.description: He (or his mount) moves up to its Speed, and he makes one Soul Blade attack.

legendaryActions.name: Lord's Call
legendaryActions.description: Summons two obedient Wights within 30 feet that act right after him for 1 hour, until either dies, or until he uses this again; a creature starting its turn within 5 feet of one makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or is Frightened until the start of its next turn. Not again until the start of his next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3, or 4 in Lair.)

traits.name: Blighted Overgrowth
traits.description: While Bloodied, it has Disadvantage on attacks, Spew Blight recharges at the start of its turn, and it regains 20 Hit Points at the start of its turn if it has at least 1, unless it took Fire damage since its last turn.

traits.name: Fungal Step
traits.description: Ignores Difficult Terrain caused by plants or fungi.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Unraveled Longing
traits.description: If it sees the likeness of its long-lost love at the start of its turn, it takes 10 Psychic and has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee attack, +11, reach 10 ft.; 18 (2d10 + 7) Slashing, plus 7 (2d6) Poison if it moved at least 20 feet first, and a Large or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 17) by one of two claws.

actions.name: Project Image
actions.description: Casts Project Image without components, using Wisdom, and can use Spew Blight and Rot Stride from the image's space while it lasts.

actions.name: Spew Blight (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 17, each creature in a 60-foot Cone: 18 (4d8) Necrotic and Poisoned, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns and succeeding automatically after 1 minute; half damage only on success.

bonusActions.name: Rot Stride
bonusActions.description: Teleports up to 60 feet; its starting or ending space must hold fungus or rotting organic matter.

legendaryActions.name: Hallucinate
legendaryActions.description: Constitution save DC 17, one creature within 60 feet: affected by Confusion until the start of the beast's next turn on failure. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Impale
legendaryActions.description: Strength save DC 19, one creature it grapples (two impaled at most): 10 (3d6) Piercing, and it is now Grappled (escape DC 17) by an impaling rib and Restrained while grappled, half damage only on success. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Trample
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks; each Large or smaller creature whose space it enters makes a DC 19 Strength save or is knocked Prone. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.name: Burning Sacrifice
traits.description: If a creature willingly gives its life in fire or lava to defeat it, that creature can never be revived, and for 24 hours the behemoth has Disadvantage on D20 Tests, half Speed, Radiant Vulnerability, and no Legendary Resistance.

traits.name: Consuming Flame
traits.description: It can deal Necrotic damage instead of any Fire damage it deals.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.description: Deals double damage to objects and structures.

traits.name: Tunneler
traits.description: Burrows through solid rock at half its Burrow Speed, leaving a 20-foot-diameter tunnel.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: One Bite attack and two Claw or Blazing Boulder attacks in any combination.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee attack, +18, reach 15 ft.; 26 (3d10 + 10) Slashing plus 11 (2d10) Fire, and the target is Grappled (escape DC 20) and Restrained while grappled.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee attack, +18, reach 15 ft.; 23 (3d8 + 10) Slashing plus 5 (1d10) Fire.

actions.name: Blazing Boulder
actions.description: Ranged attack, +18, range 150 ft.; 15 (1d10 + 10) Bludgeoning plus 7 (2d6) Fire and Prone.

actions.name: Cataclysmic Spellcasting (1/Day)
actions.description: Casts Earthquake and Meteor Swarm without Material components, using Charisma (save DC 24).

reactions.name: Hellish Rebuke
reactions.description: Casts Hellish Rebuke in response to its trigger, using Charisma.

legendaryActions.name: Fire Rain
legendaryActions.description: One Blazing Boulder attack.

legendaryActions.name: Lava Well
legendaryActions.description: Lava fills its space and any open spaces in tunnels it dug within 100 feet; a creature touching it for the first time on a turn or starting its turn in it takes 55 (10d10) Fire, once per round. It hardens after 1 hour or when this is used again. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Trample
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed and makes one Claw attack, knocking a creature it hits Prone. (Legendary Action Uses: 3, or 4 in Lair.)

display.damageResistances: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, Thunder
display.conditionImmunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

traits.name: Ancestral Shame
traits.description: A creature within 30 feet that speaks Orc and uses an action to read aloud the names carved on the stone on its back deals it 20 Radiant.

traits.name: Ethereal Sight
traits.description: Sees 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: Moves through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain, taking 5 (1d10) Force if it ends its turn inside an object.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: One Balefire Scythe and one Chain attack, then Chain Slam or Fling.

actions.name: Balefire Scythe
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 15 ft.; 14 (2d8 + 5) Necrotic, and the target starts burning, taking Necrotic instead of Fire damage from it.

actions.name: Chain
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 20 ft.; 16 (2d10 + 5) Piercing, and a Large or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 15) by one of four chains.

actions.name: Chain Slam
actions.description: Constitution save DC 17, each creature it grapples: 9 (1d8 + 5) Bludgeoning and Stunned until the start of its next turn, half damage only on success.

actions.name: Etherealness
actions.description: Casts Etherealness without components, using Charisma; it stays visible across the Border Ethereal and Material Plane but can't affect or be affected across them.

actions.name: Fling
actions.description: Throws a Large or smaller creature it grapples to a grounded space within 30 feet; the thrown creature and each creature there make a DC 17 Dexterity save, taking 9 (2d8) Bludgeoning and falling Prone, half damage only on success.

legendaryActions.name: Balefire Scythe
legendaryActions.description: One Balefire Scythe attack.

legendaryActions.name: Drift
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendaryActions.name: Lantern Flare
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 17, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation: Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks until the end of its next turn on failure. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.name: Honor Lost
traits.description: A creature that uses a Bonus Action to present a memento or reminder of his past and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check gives him Disadvantage on his next D20 Test before its next turn.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If he fails a save, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Spider Climb
traits.description: Can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check.

traits.name: Sunlight Hypersensitivity
traits.description: Takes 20 Radiant if he starts his turn in sunlight, and has Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks there.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Sanguine Blade attacks; he can replace one with Blood Call.

actions.name: Sanguine Blade
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 5 ft.; 11 (1d10 + 6) Slashing plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic.

actions.name: Blood Call
actions.description: Constitution save DC 15, one non-Construct, non-Undead creature within 30 feet: 7 (2d6) Necrotic and its Hit Point maximum drops by that much, half damage only on success; he regains Hit Points equal to the damage. A Humanoid killed this way and buried rises at the next sunset as a Crimson Clergy under his control.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Charisma, save DC 15, no Material components. At will: Command, Disguise Self (as a Medium Humanoid, 24-hour duration), Thaumaturgy. 1/day: Word of Recall (to lair only).

reactions.name: Parry
reactions.description: Adds 3 to his AC against an attack that hits him while he holds a weapon, possibly causing a miss.

legendaryActions.name: Bloody Strike
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half his Speed and makes one Sanguine Blade attack.

legendaryActions.name: Castigate
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 15, one creature within 60 feet: Frightened, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns and succeeding automatically after 1 minute.

legendaryActions.name: Overwhelm
legendaryActions.description: Casts Command. Not again until the start of his next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

display.conditionImmunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned

traits.name: Death's Shroud
traits.description: She is always Invisible, even to Blindsight, Truesight, and similar effects, but a creature that has ever been reduced to 0 Hit Points sees her normally.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.description: Moves through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain, taking 5 (1d10) Force if she ends her turn inside an object.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If she fails a save, she can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Steadfast Matron
traits.description: Undead of her choice (not herself) in her 60-foot Emanation have Advantage on saves, unless she is Incapacitated.

traits.name: Undeniable Guilt
traits.description: If at the start of her turn she sees a possession of her living children or sees or hears her children's spirits, she is Incapacitated until her next turn and must move as far away from them as possible.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Three Shears attacks.

actions.name: Shears
actions.description: Melee attack, +14, reach 5 ft.; 25 (4d8 + 7) Force. A creature hit by two or more Shears attacks in a turn gains 1 Exhaustion level.

actions.name: Mournful Tolling (1/Day)
actions.description: Wisdom save DC 22, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation (Constructs, Undead, and creatures ever raised from the dead succeed automatically): 77 (14d10) Psychic that ignores Resistance and Stunned until the end of her next turn, half damage only on success.

bonusActions.name: Soul Doll
bonusActions.description: Draws the soul from the corpse of a creature she killed in the last minute into a Tiny ceramic doll of it (AC 15, Hit Points equal to half the creature's maximum, Vulnerability to Thunder, immunity to Poison). The soul dimly perceives its surroundings and can speak telepathically. If the doll breaks, the soul rises as a Shadow under her control; the creature can be revived only after Wish frees the soul or the Shadow it spawned is destroyed.

legendaryActions.name: Drift
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks; each creature whose space she enters takes 16 (3d10) Cold (once per turn) and has Disadvantage on its next attack before the end of its next turn. Not again until the start of her next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Endless Keening
legendaryActions.description: Constitution save DC 22, each non-Deafened creature in a 30-foot Emanation (Constructs, Undead, and creatures ever raised from the dead succeed automatically): 28 (8d6) Necrotic that ignores Resistance, half on success, or 0 Hit Points on a failure by 5 or more. Not again until the start of her next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Snip
legendaryActions.description: One Shears attack. (Legendary Action Uses: 3, or 4 in Lair.)

traits.name: Binding Skull
traits.description: It is Vulnerable to all damage from a creature holding its original skull and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks against that creature.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Headsman's Axe attacks and one Hooves attack.

actions.name: Headsman's Axe
actions.description: Melee attack, +12, reach 5 ft.; 19 (2d12 + 6) Slashing plus 16 (3d10) Fire. On a roll of 20 against a creature with a head, the target makes a DC 20 Constitution save or is decapitated, dying if it can't live without a head; a creature that took no damage, has Legendary Actions, or is Huge or larger instead takes an extra 28 (8d6) Force.

actions.name: Hooves
actions.description: Melee attack, +12, reach 5 ft.; 24 (4d8 + 6) Bludgeoning, plus 9 (2d8) Necrotic and Prone if it moved at least 20 feet first.

actions.name: Flaming Skull (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Hurls its skull, which then returns to its hand: Dexterity save DC 20, each creature in a 90-foot by 10-foot Line, 63 (14d8) Fire, half on success, and every target starts burning.

legendaryActions.name: Move
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendaryActions.name: Rancorous Gaze
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 18, one creature it can see within 90 feet: Frightened, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns and succeeding automatically after 1 minute. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Relentless Execution
legendaryActions.description: One Headsman's Axe attack with Advantage, treating a 19 as a 20 against a Frightened target. Not again until the start of its next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3, or 4 in Lair.)

display.languages: understands all languages but can't speak

traits.name: Crooked Switch (1/Day)
traits.description: When it becomes Bloodied, it regains all Legendary Resistance uses and turns malevolent (Chaotic Evil) for 12 hours, during which it can use Multiattack.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack (Crooked Switch Only)
actions.description: Two Rail Slam attacks.

actions.name: Rail Slam
actions.description: Melee attack, +6, reach 10 ft.; 9 (1d10 + 4) Bludgeoning, and the target is pushed up to 10 feet straight away.

actions.name: Spirit Exhaust (Recharge 6)
actions.description: Constitution save DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone: 10 (3d6) Necrotic, half on success.

legendaryActions.name: Ghostly Rails
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed in a straight line without provoking Opportunity Attacks; each Large or smaller creature whose space it passes through is Grappled (escape DC 14) by spectral rails.

legendaryActions.name: Haunting Whistle
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 13, one creature within 30 feet: 4 (1d8) Psychic and Frightened until the end of its next turn on failure. Not again until the start of its next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

display.senses: darkvision 120 ft. (unimpeded by magical Darkness); passive Perception 13

traits.name: Coffin Rider
traits.description: His magic coffin is immune to all damage; standing on it, he rides a ghostly wave of swamp water at Speed 60 and can move over liquids as if solid.

traits.name: Curse Bottle
traits.description: His bottle of cursed magic has AC 15, 25 Hit Points, and immunity to all damage but Force; if destroyed, he makes a new one when he finishes a Long Rest.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If he fails a save, he can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Overweening Pride
traits.description: A creature can use a Bonus Action to insult his piratical skill and renown; he makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or takes 10 Psychic and has Disadvantage on attacks against anyone else.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two attacks using Hex Grasp or Blunderbuss in any combination; he can replace one with Spellcasting to cast Bane.

actions.name: Hex Grasp
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 5 ft.; 12 (2d6 + 5) Necrotic, and a creature is cursed until the start of his next turn or until he curses it again, with Disadvantage on attacks and on checks using an ability of his choice.

actions.name: Blunderbuss
actions.description: Ranged attack, +9, range 30/90 ft.; 18 (3d8 + 5) Force, and a Large or smaller target is pushed up to 10 feet.

actions.name: Curse Blast (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: One curse from his blunderbuss: Jack's Anguish (DC 17 Wisdom save, 30-foot Cone: 11 (2d10) Psychic and Frightened, repeating the save each turn end and succeeding automatically after 1 minute; half damage only on success) or Shadowy Friends (DC 17 Dexterity save, 15-foot Cone: Paralyzed until the end of his next turn or until it takes damage).

actions.name: Spellcasting (Requires Curse Bottle)
actions.description: Charisma, save DC 17, using the bottle as the only Material component. At will: Bane, Bestow Curse, Major Image, Remove Curse. 1/day each: Animate Dead, Creation, Darkness.

legendaryActions.name: Barbed Curse
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 17, one creature within 30 feet that he has cursed or that is under his Bane: 6 (1d12) Force on failure.

legendaryActions.name: Grinning Grasp
legendaryActions.description: Teleports to a space he can see within 30 feet and makes one Hex Grasp attack before or after. Not again until the start of his next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Jinxed Ground
legendaryActions.description: Charisma save DC 17, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation: Prone on failure. Not again until the start of his next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

display.senses: blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 120 ft.; passive Perception 18

traits.name: Demonic Mimicry
traits.description: Mimics voices and sounds it has heard; a DC 18 Wisdom (Insight) check reveals the imitation.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Unraveling Song
traits.description: A creature that plays or sings Jericho Sticks' favorite song, "Coal-Eyed Birds," as an Influence action Charms it until the end of that creature's next turn, ending early if the creature damages it or forces it to save.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: One Claw and one Scythe attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee attack, +7, reach 5 ft.; 8 (1d8 + 4) Slashing, and a Medium or smaller target is knocked Prone.

actions.name: Scythe
actions.description: Melee attack, +7, reach 10 ft.; 9 (1d10 + 4) Slashing plus 4 (1d8) Psychic.

actions.name: Dirge of Secrets (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Wisdom save DC 15, each creature in a 30-foot Emanation: 11 (2d10) Psychic and Disadvantage on ability checks and attacks, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns and succeeding automatically after 1 minute; half damage only on success.

legendaryActions.name: Averting Winds
legendaryActions.description: Casts Wind Wall (not in a creature's space) without components, using Charisma.

legendaryActions.name: Crow's Swoop
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendaryActions.name: Devour Secrets
legendaryActions.description: Wisdom save DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation (Disadvantage for one that has given it a secret): 7 (2d6) Psychic and Speed 0 until the end of its next turn, half damage only on success. Not again until the start of its next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.name: Enduring Restoration
traits.description: If it dies, its body vanishes in ash and it becomes an intangible, Invisible spirit in its home forest, unable to form a new body for 10d10 years.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (5/Day)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Cursed Strike
actions.description: Melee attack, +12 (Critical Hit on 19 or 20 against a cursed target), reach 10 ft.; 17 (2d10 + 6) Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing (its choice) plus 7 (2d6) Necrotic, and a creature is cursed until the end of its next turn, subtracting 1d4 from D20 Tests.

actions.name: Breath of Corruption (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 19, each creature in a 60-foot Cone: 21 (6d6) Necrotic plus 21 (6d6) Psychic and 1 Exhaustion level that ends at the end of its next turn, half damage only on success.

actions.name: Terrorizing Breath
actions.description: Wisdom save DC 19, each creature in a 60-foot Cone: Frightened, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns and succeeding automatically after 1 minute.

bonusActions.name: Sense Desire
bonusActions.description: Casts Detect Thoughts without components, using Charisma (save DC 20).

legendaryActions.name: Taste of Wickedness
legendaryActions.description: Charisma save DC 20, one cursed creature it can see within 15 feet: 16 (3d10) Psychic, it regains that many Hit Points, and one of its curses on the target ends.

legendaryActions.name: Temptation
legendaryActions.description: Offers a creature it can see within 120 feet Heroic Inspiration or 20 Hit Points; if accepted, the creature is cursed for 1 minute, and the king has Resistance to all its damage. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Trample
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed and makes one Cursed Strike attack. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.description: Can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day, or 5/Day in Lair)
traits.description: If it fails a save, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Returned Curse
traits.description: If it curses a creature holding an idol of Snake Eye Jack blessed by one of his devotees, the creature is unaffected and the leviathan takes 20 Radiant and has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: One Bite and one Tail attack.

actions.description: Melee attack, +17, reach 15 ft.; 23 (2d12 + 10) Piercing plus 13 (3d8) Force, and the target is Grappled (escape DC 20) and Restrained while grappled.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee attack, +17, reach 20 ft.; 23 (3d8 + 10) Bludgeoning, and a Huge or smaller target is knocked Prone and pushed up to 20 feet away.

actions.name: Accursed Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 22, each creature in a 120-foot by 10-foot Line: 78 (12d12) Necrotic and cursed (Disadvantage on D20 Tests and no healing, ending early if it voluntarily fails a save an enemy forces), half damage only on success.

actions.name: Swallow
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 25, one Large or smaller creature it grapples (up to four swallowed): on failure it is swallowed, Restrained, with Total Cover from outside, taking 24 (7d6) Force at the start of each of its turns. If it takes 50 or more damage in one turn from inside, it makes a DC 25 Constitution save at the end of that turn or regurgitates everyone Prone within 10 feet; if it dies, they can escape using 15 feet of movement, exiting Prone. Not again until the start of its next turn.

reactions.name: Jinxed Hide
reactions.description: When a creature within 60 feet hits it with an attack or targets it with a spell, that creature makes a DC 20 Wisdom save or is cursed until the end of its next turn, with Disadvantage on D20 Tests and unable to regain Hit Points.

legendaryActions.name: Devour
legendaryActions.description: One Bite attack or Swallow. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Swamp Surge
legendaryActions.description: Strength save DC 20, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation: 21 (6d6) Bludgeoning and Speed 0 until the end of its next turn, half damage only on success. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Tail Sweep
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and makes one Tail attack. (Legendary Action Uses: 3, or 4 in Lair.)

traits.name: Bitter Medicine
traits.description: A creature that uses a Bonus Action to belittle his humor and succeeds on a DC 16 Charisma (Deception) check gives him Disadvantage on attacks against anyone else until the start of its next turn.

traits.name: Infinite Jest
traits.description: He creates an insubstantial illusory Small jester in his space that he can move up to 60 feet each turn unless Incapacitated, perceiving and speaking through it; it can manipulate objects as if it had Strength 10.

actions.name: Joy Buzzer
actions.description: His jester moves to the target. Melee or ranged attack, +10, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft.; 24 (3d12 + 5) Lightning, and the target can't take Reactions until the end of his next turn. Hit or miss, the jester then returns to his space.

actions.name: Exploding Pie (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Dexterity save DC 18, each creature in a 20-foot Sphere on a point within 100 feet: 16 (3d10) Acid and Blinded until the end of his next turn, half damage only on success.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Charisma, save DC 19, no Material components. At will: Hideous Laughter, Project Image (as a Small jester), Vicious Mockery (4d6 Psychic). 1/day each: Irresistible Dance, Magnificent Mansion.

bonusActions.name: Ribbon Step
bonusActions.description: Vanishes in confetti and teleports to an unoccupied space he can see within 30 feet.

legendaryActions.name: Frolic
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to half his Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks, passing through creatures at no extra cost; each creature whose space he enters takes 7 (2d6) Psychic once per turn.

legendaryActions.name: Joke's on You
legendaryActions.description: Uses Spellcasting to cast Irresistible Dance or Vicious Mockery.

legendaryActions.name: Ribbon Dance
legendaryActions.description: Strength save DC 18, each creature he grapples: 22 (4d10) Bludgeoning, half on success. Not again until the start of his next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.description: Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects.

traits.description: A creature can use a Bonus Action to dance steps from his court and make a DC 20 Charisma (Performance) check; on a success he takes 20 Force and has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the start of that creature's next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Claw attacks, and he uses Spellcasting to cast Vicious Mockery (4d6 Psychic).

actions.description: Melee attack, +12, reach 15 ft.; 13 (2d6 + 6) Slashing plus 14 (4d6) Psychic, and a Large or smaller target is Grappled (escape DC 14) by one of two claws and Restrained while grappled.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Charisma, save DC 19, no Material components. At will: Invisibility, Minor Illusion, Vicious Mockery (4d6 Psychic). 2/day: Darkness.

bonusActions.name: Elusive Disguise
bonusActions.description: Transforms into a Small or Medium Humanoid of any features, always unnaturally tall, or back, keeping his statistics except size; his gear adapts, and he reverts on death.

reactions.name: Evasive Blink
reactions.description: When he takes damage, he gains Resistance to it and teleports up to 30 feet to a space he can see.

traits.description: It has three heads (centipede hag, pigeon hag, weasel hag). Whenever it takes 50 or more damage in one turn, a random head dies; it dies when all are dead. At the end of each of its turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point and a dead head, it regains 20 Hit Points and one dead head revives.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Three attacks using Cauldron Slam or Brew Spray in any combination.

actions.name: Cauldron Slam
actions.description: Melee attack, +9, reach 5 ft.; 11 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning plus 9 (2d8) Acid.

actions.name: Brew Spray
actions.description: Ranged attack, +7, range 90 ft.; 20 (4d8 + 2) Acid, and the target takes a -2 penalty to AC until the end of the abomination's next turn.

actions.name: Spellcasting
actions.description: Charisma, save DC 18, no Material components. At will: Dispel Magic, Hypnotic Pattern. 1/day each: Contagion, Dominate Person, Dream.

legendaryActions.name: Corrosive Teleport
legendaryActions.description: Teleports up to 60 feet to a space it can see; each creature in a 10-foot Emanation at the destination makes a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 7 (2d6) Acid or half on success.

legendaryActions.name: Crushing Leap
legendaryActions.description: Jumps to a space within 30 feet holding Large or smaller creatures; each there makes a DC 17 Dexterity save: 15 (2d10 + 4) Bludgeoning and Prone, or half damage and pushed 5 feet away on success. Not again until the start of its next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Hag's Head
legendaryActions.description: One option from a living head, each not again until the start of its next turn: Contagious Miasma (centipede; DC 18 Constitution save, one creature within 5 feet: 13 (3d8) Poison and Poisoned, unable to heal while Poisoned, resaving after each Long Rest; half damage only on success); Overwhelming Doubt (pigeon; DC 18 Wisdom save, one creature within 30 feet: 10 (3d6) Psychic and Incapacitated until the end of its next turn, half damage only on success); Waking Nightmare (weasel; DC 18 Charisma save, one creature within 30 feet: 11 (2d10) Psychic and Frightened, seeing its allies as enemies though not compelled to act, repeating the save each turn end and succeeding automatically after 1 minute; half damage only on success). (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.description: If she fails a save, she can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Reopened Memories
traits.description: If at the start of her turn she sees a memento of her husband or another reminder of her loss, she has Disadvantage on D20 Tests and can spend only 2 Legendary Action uses until her next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Two Injection attacks.

actions.name: Injection
actions.description: Melee or ranged attack, +8, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft.; 1 Piercing plus 10 (3d6) Poison, and a creature is Poisoned until the end of its next turn with one effect of her choice (each once per turn): Hyperphobic Stimulant (Frightened, and at the start of its turn it makes a DC 16 Wisdom save or Dashes away from her by the safest route); Soporific Infusion (DC 16 Constitution save or Speed halved, only an action or a Bonus Action each turn, and one attack per Attack action, or Unconscious for 1 minute, until damaged, or until shaken awake on a failure by 5 or more); Thaumaturgic Inhibitor (when it casts a spell, it makes a DC 16 Constitution save or the spell fails without expending the slot).

legendaryActions.name: Alacrity
legendaryActions.description: She or a creature she is riding moves up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendaryActions.name: Dose
legendaryActions.description: One Injection attack. Not again until the start of her next turn.

legendaryActions.name: Hypertrophic Injections
legendaryActions.description: She or an ally within 5 feet gains one effect: Aggression (Advantage on attacks until the end of its next turn), Fortitude (ends one of Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Poisoned, Restrained, or Stunned), or Vigor (regains 10 Hit Points). Not again until the start of her next turn. (Legendary Action Uses: 3.)

At 0 Hit Points the target is Stable but loses all memories permanently (only Wish restores them), and the worm reappears within 60 feet. It also ends if the target uses an action on a DC 20 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma check and the worm then fails a Charisma save against that total; if the target receives an effect that ends possession, such as Dispel Evil and Good; or when the target takes damage, the worm takes half as much Psychic and fails a Charisma save with DC equal to that damage.

legendaryActions.name: Slither
legendaryActions.description: Moves up to its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Anything that ends the Poisoned condition, or 10 or more Poison damage dealt to the host, kills the worms. Not again until the start of its next turn.

display.description: On your turn, you can take one action. Choose which action to take from those below or from the special actions provided by your features.

When you take the Attack action, you can make one attack roll with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

Equipping and Unequipping Weapons. You can either equip or unequip one weapon when you make an attack as part of this action. You do so either before or after the attack. If you equip a weapon before an attack, you don't need to use it for that attack. Equipping a weapon includes drawing it from a sheath or picking it up. Unequipping a weapon includes sheathing, stowing, or dropping it.

Moving between Attacks. If you move on your turn and have a feature, such as Extra Attack, that gives you more than one attack as part of the Attack action, you can use some or all of that movement to move between those attacks.

When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your Speed after applying any modifiers. With a Speed of 30 feet, for example, you can move up to 60 feet on your turn if you Dash. If your Speed of 30 feet is reduced to 15 feet, you can move up to 30 feet this turn if you Dash.

If you have a special speed, such as a Fly Speed or Swim Speed, you can use that speed instead of your Speed when you take this action. You choose which speed to use each time you take it.
If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the current turn.

If you take the Dodge action, you gain the following benefits: until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has Disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with Advantage.

You lose these benefits if you have the Incapacitated condition or if your Speed is 0.

When you take the Help action, you do one of the following.

Assist an Ability Check. Choose one of your skill or tool proficiencies and one ally who is near
enough for you to assist verbally or physically when they make an ability check. That ally has Advantage on the next ability check they make with the chosen skill or tool. This benefit expires if the ally doesn't use it before the start of your next turn. The GM has final say on whether your assistance is possible.

Assist an Attack Roll. You momentarily distract an enemy within 5 feet of you, giving Advantage to the next attack roll by one of your allies against that enemy. This benefit expires at the start of your next turn.

With the Hide action, you try to hide yourself. To do so, you must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check while you're Heavily Obscured or behind Three-Quarters Cover or Total Cover, and you must be out of any enemy's line of sight; if you can see a creature, you can discern whether it can see you.

On a successful check, you have the Invisible condition while hidden. Make note of your check's total, which is the DC for a creature to find you with a Wisdom (Perception) check.

You stop being hidden immediately after any of the following occurs: you make a sound louder than a whisper, an enemy finds you, you make an attack roll, or you cast a spell with a Verbal component.

With the Influence action, you urge a monster to do something. Describe or roleplay how you're communicating with the monster. Are you trying to deceive, intimidate, amuse, or gently persuade? The GM then determines whether the monster feels willing, unwilling, or hesitant due to your interaction; this determination establishes whether an ability check is necessary, as explained below.

Willing. If your urging aligns with the monster's desires, no ability check is necessary; the monster fulfills your request in a way it prefers.

Unwilling. If your urging is repugnant to the monster or counter to its alignment, no ability check is necessary; it doesn't comply.

Hesitant. If you urge the monster to do something that it is hesitant to do, you must make an ability check, which is affected by the monster's attitude: Indifferent, Friendly, or Hostile, each of which is defined in this glossary. The Influence Checks table suggests which ability check to make based on how you're interacting with the monster. The GM chooses the check, which has a default DC equal to 15 or the monster's Intelligence score, whichever is higher. On a successful check, the monster does as urged. On a failed check, you must wait 24 hours (or a duration set by the GM) before urging it in the same way again.

Influence Checks

When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.

If you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 minute or longer, you must take the Magic action on each turn of that casting, and you must maintain Concentration while you do so. If your Concentration is broken, the spell fails, but you don't expend a spell slot.

You take the Ready action to wait for a particular circumstance before you act. To do so, you take this action on your turn, which lets you act by taking a Reaction before the start of your next turn.

First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your Reaction. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your Speed in response to it. Examples include "If the cultist steps on the
trapdoor, I'll pull the lever that opens it," and "If the zombie steps next to me, I move away."

When the trigger occurs, you can either take your Reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger.

When you Ready a spell, you cast it as normal (expending any resources used to cast it) but hold its energy, which you release with your Reaction when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a spell must have a casting time of an action, and holding on to the spell's magic requires Concentration, which you can maintain up to the start of your next turn. If your Concentration is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect.

When you take the Search action, you make a Wisdom check to discern something that isn't obvious. The Search table suggests which skills are applicable when you take this action, depending on what you're trying to detect.

Search

When you take the Study action, you make an Intelligence check to study your memory, a book, a clue, or another source of knowledge and call to mind an important piece of information about it.

The Areas of Knowledge table suggests which skills are applicable to various areas of knowledge.

Areas of Knowledge

You normally interact with an object while doing something else, such as when you draw a sword as part of the Attack action. When an object requires an action for its use, you take the Utilize action.

A Bonus Action is a special action that you can take on the same turn that you take an action. You can't take more than one Bonus Action on a turn, and you have a Bonus Action to take only if a rule explicitly says so.

A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description. You can take a Reaction on another creature's turn, and if you take it on your turn, you can do so even if you also take an action, a Bonus Action, or both. Once you take a Reaction, you can't take another one until the start of your next turn. The Opportunity Attack is a Reaction available to all creatures.

You can make an Opportunity Attack when a creature that you can see leaves your reach using its action, its Bonus Action, its Reaction, or one of its speeds. To make the Opportunity Attack, take a Reaction to make one melee attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

Instead of using a weapon to make a melee attack, you can use a punch, kick, headbutt, or similar forceful blow. In game terms, this is an Unarmed Strike - a melee attack that involves you using your body to damage, grapple, or shove a target within 5 feet of you.

Whenever you use your Unarmed Strike, choose one of the following options for its effect.

Damage. You make an attack roll against the target. Your bonus to the roll equals your Strength modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to 1 plus your Strength modifier.

Grapple. The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it chooses which), or it has the Grappled condition. The DC for the saving throw and any escape attempts equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus. This grapple is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you and if you have a hand free to grab it.

Shove. The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it chooses which), or you either push it 5 feet away or cause it to have the Prone condition. The DC for the saving throw equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus. This shove is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you.

A creature can grapple another creature. Characters typically grapple by using an Unarmed Strike. Many monsters have special attacks that allow them to quickly grapple prey. However a grapple is initiated, it follows these rules.

Grappled Condition. Successfully grappling a creature gives it the Grappled condition.

One Grapple per Hand. A creature must have a hand free to grapple another creature. Some stat blocks and game effects allow a creature to grapple using a tentacle, a maw, or another body part. Whatever part a grappler uses, it can grapple only one creature at a time with that part, and the grappler can't use that part to target another creature unless it ends the grapple.

Ending a Grapple. A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the grapple's escape DC, ending the condition on itself on a success. The condition also ends if the grappler has the Incapacitated condition or if the distance between the Grappled target and the grappler exceeds the grapple's range. In addition, the grappler can release the target at any time (no action required).

Cover provides a degree of protection to a target behind it. There are three degrees of cover, each of which provides a different benefit to a target: Half Cover (+2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws), Three-Quarters Cover (+5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws), and Total Cover (can't be targeted directly). If behind more than one degree of cover, a target benefits only from the most protective degree.

If you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll, you score a Critical Hit, and the attack hits regardless of any modifiers or the target's AC. A Critical Hit lets you roll extra dice for the attack's damage against the target. Roll all of the attack's damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers.
If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). Resistance is applied only once to an instance of damage.
If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you. Vulnerability is applied only once to an instance of damage.
If you have Immunity to a damage type or a condition, it doesn't affect you in any way.

A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has Immunity to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage. Any damage that fails to meet or exceed the damage threshold is superficial and doesn't reduce Hit Points. For example, if an object has a damage threshold of 10, the object takes no damage if 9 damage is dealt to it, since that damage fails to exceed the threshold. If the same object is dealt 11 damage, it takes all of that damage.

When you would reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, you can instead reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point. The creature then has the Unconscious condition and starts a Short Rest.

The creature remains Unconscious until it regains any Hit Points or until someone uses an action to administer first aid to it, which requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check.

An improvised weapon is an object wielded as a makeshift weapon, such as broken glass, a table leg, or a frying pan. A Simple or Martial weapon also counts as an improvised weapon if it's wielded in a way contrary to its design; if you use a Ranged weapon to make a melee attack or throw a Melee weapon that lacks the Thrown property, the weapon counts as an improvised weapon. An improvised weapon follows the rules below.

Proficiency. Don't add your Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls with an improvised weapon.

Damage. On a hit, the weapon deals 1d4 damage of a type the GM thinks is appropriate for the object.

Range. If you throw the weapon, it has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

Weapon Equivalents. If an improvised weapon resembles a Simple or Martial weapon, the GM may say it functions as that weapon and uses that weapon's rules. For example, the GM could treat a table leg as a Club.

Initiative determines the order of turns during combat. The combat rules in "Playing the Game" explain how to roll Initiative.

Sometimes a GM might have combatants use their Initiative scores instead of rolling Initiative. Your Initiative score equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier. If you have Advantage on Initiative rolls, increase your Initiative score by 5. If you have Disadvantage on those rolls, decrease that score by 5.
If a creature is caught unawares by the start of combat, that creature is surprised, which causes it to have Disadvantage on its Initiative roll.
A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining.
A player character must make a Death Saving Throw (also called a Death Save) if they start their turn with 0 Hit Points.
A creature is Stable if it has 0 Hit Points but isn't required to make Death Saving Throws.
Temporary Hit Points are granted by certain effects and act as a buffer against losing real Hit Points.

If a space is Difficult Terrain, every foot of movement in that space costs 1 extra foot. For example, moving 5 feet through Difficult Terrain costs 10 feet of movement. Difficult Terrain isn't cumulative; either a space is Difficult Terrain or it isn't.

A space is Difficult Terrain if the space contains any of the following or something similar:

- A creature that isn't Tiny or your ally
- Furniture that is sized for creatures of your size or larger
- Heavy snow, ice, rubble, or undergrowth
- Liquid that's between shin- and waist-deep
- A narrow opening sized for a creature one size smaller than you
- A slope of 20 degrees or more
When you jump, you make either a Long Jump (horizontal) or a High Jump (vertical).

A creature that falls takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage at the end of the fall for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d6. When the creature lands, it has the Prone condition unless it avoids taking any damage from the fall.

A creature that falls into water or another liquid can use its Reaction to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to hit the surface head or feet first. On a successful check, any damage resulting from the fall is halved.

A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 plus its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds) before suffocation begins. When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each of its turns. When a creature can breathe again, it removes all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating.

A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns. As an action, you can extinguish fire on yourself by giving yourself the Prone condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

A creature requires an amount of water per day based on its size, as shown in the Water Needs per Day table. A creature that drinks less than half the required water for a day gains 1 Exhaustion level at the day's end. Exhaustion caused by dehydration can't be removed until the creature drinks the full amount of water required for a day.

Water Needs per Day

A creature needs an amount of food per day based on its size, as shown in the Food Needs per Day table. A creature that eats but consumes less than half the required food for a day must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion level at the day's end. A creature that eats nothing for 5 days automatically gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of the fifth day as well as an additional level at the end of each subsequent day without food.

Exhaustion caused by malnutrition can't be removed until the creature eats the full amount of food required for a day.

Food Needs per Day
You have the Blinded condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space.
You have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to see something in a Lightly Obscured space.
Bright Light is normal illumination.
An area with Dim Light is Lightly Obscured.
An area of Darkness is Heavily Obscured.

If you have Darkvision, you can see in Dim Light within a specified range as if it were Bright Light and in Darkness within that range as if it were Dim Light. You discern colors in that Darkness only as shades of gray.

If you have Blindsight, you can see within a specific range without relying on physical sight. Within that range, you can see anything that isn't behind Total Cover even if you have the Blinded condition or are in Darkness. Moreover, in that range, you can see something that has the Invisible condition.

If you have Truesight, your vision is enhanced within a specified range. Within that range, your vision pierces through the following:

Darkness. You can see in normal and magical Darkness.

Invisibility. You see creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition.

Visual Illusions. Visual illusions appear transparent to you, and you automatically succeed on saving throws against them.

Transformations. You discern the true form of any creature or object you see that has been transformed by magic.

Ethereal Plane. You see into the Ethereal Plane.

A Short Rest is a 1-hour period of downtime, during which a creature does nothing more strenuous than reading, talking, eating, or standing watch. To start a Short Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point.

Benefits of the Rest. When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

Spend Hit Point Dice. You can spend one or more of your Hit Point Dice to regain Hit Points. For each Hit Point Die you spend in this way, roll the die and add your Constitution modifier to it. You regain Hit Points equal to the total (minimum of 1 Hit Point). You can decide to spend an additional Hit Point Die after each roll.

Special Feature. Some features are recharged by a Short Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

Interrupting the Rest. A Short Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

- Rolling Initiative
- Casting a spell other than a cantrip
- Taking any damage

An interrupted Short Rest confers no benefits.

A Long Rest is a period of extended downtime - at least 8 hours - available to any creature. During a Long Rest, you sleep for at least 6 hours and perform no more than 2 hours of light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch.

During sleep, you have the Unconscious condition. After you finish a Long Rest, you must wait at least 16 hours before starting another one.

Benefits of the Rest. To start a Long Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point. When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

Regain All HP. You regain all lost Hit Points and all spent Hit Point Dice. If your Hit Point maximum was reduced, it returns to normal.

Ability Scores Restored. If any of your ability scores were reduced, they return to normal.

Exhaustion Reduced. If you have the Exhaustion condition, its level decreases by 1.

Special Feature. Some features are recharged by a Long Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

Interrupting the Rest. A Long Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

- Rolling Initiative
- Casting a spell other than a cantrip
- Taking any damage
- 1 hour of walking or other physical exertion

If you rested at least 1 hour before the interruption, you gain the benefits of a Short Rest.

You can resume a Long Rest immediately after an interruption. If you do so, the rest requires 1 additional hour per interruption to finish.

Some spells and other effects require Concentration to remain active, as specified in their descriptions. If the effect's creator loses Concentration, the effect ends. If the effect has a maximum duration, the effect's description specifies how long the creator can concentrate on it: up to 1 minute, 1 hour, or some other duration. The creator can end Concentration at any time (no action required). The following factors break Concentration.

Another Concentration Effect. You lose Concentration on an effect the moment you start casting a spell that requires Concentration or activate another effect that requires Concentration.

Damage. If you take damage, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration. The DC equals 10 or half the damage taken (round down), whichever number is higher, up to a maximum DC of 30.

Incapacitated or Dead. Your Concentration ends if you have the Incapacitated condition or you die.

The descriptions of many spells and other features specify that they have an area of effect, which typically has one of six shapes. These shapes are defined elsewhere in this glossary:

An area of effect has a point of origin, a location from which the effect's energy erupts. The rules for each shape specify how to position its point of origin. If all straight lines extending from the point of origin to a location in the area of effect are blocked, that location isn't included in the area of effect. To block a line, an obstruction must provide Total Cover.

If the creator of an area of effect places it at an unseen point and an obstruction - such as a wall - is between the creator and that point, the point of origin comes into being on the near side of the obstruction.
A spell attack is an attack roll made as part of a spell or another magical effect.

If you have a spell prepared that has the Ritual tag, you can cast that spell as a Ritual. The Ritual version of a spell takes 10 minutes longer to cast than normal. It also doesn't expend a spell slot, which means the ritual version of a spell can't be cast at a higher level.

Some magic items require a creature to form a bond - called Attunement - with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. A creature can have Attunement with no more than three magic items at a time.
If you have Advantage on a D20 Test, roll two d20s, and use the higher roll. A roll can't be affected by more than one Advantage, and Advantage and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other.

If you have Disadvantage on a D20 Test, roll two d20s and use the lower roll. A roll can't be affected by more than one Disadvantage, and Advantage and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other.

Passive Perception is a score that reflects a creature's general awareness of its surroundings. The GM uses this score when determining whether a creature notices something without consciously making a Wisdom (Perception) check.

A creature's Passive Perception equals 10 plus the creature's Wisdom (Perception) check bonus. If the creature has Advantage on such checks, increase the score by 5. If the creature has Disadvantage on them, decrease the score by 5. For example, a level 1 character with a Wisdom of 15 and proficiency in Perception has a Passive Perception of 14 (10 + 2 + 2). If that character has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks, the score becomes 19.

If you (a player character) have Heroic Inspiration, you can expend it to reroll any die immediately after rolling it, and you must use the new roll.

If you gain Heroic Inspiration but already have it, it's lost unless you give it to a player character who lacks it.

Aiming a ranged attack is more difficult when a foe is next to you. When you make a ranged attack roll with a weapon, a spell, or some other means, you have Disadvantage on the roll if you are within 5 feet of an enemy who can see you and doesn't have the Incapacitated condition (see "Rules Glossary").

You can make ranged attacks only against targets within a specified range. If a ranged attack, such as one made with a spell, has a single range, you can't attack a target beyond this range.

Some ranged attacks, such as those made with a Longbow, have two ranges. The smaller number is the normal range, and the larger number is the long range. Your attack roll has Disadvantage when your target is beyond normal range, and you can't attack a target beyond long range.

You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.
When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.
You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.
You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.
A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.
A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.
A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

If you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using this weapon, you can make a melee attack roll with the weapon against a second creature within 5 feet of the first that is also within your reach. On a hit, the second creature takes the weapon's damage, but don't add your ability modifier to that damage unless that modifier is negative. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.

If your attack roll with this weapon misses a creature, you can deal damage to that creature equal to the ability modifier you used to make the attack roll. This damage is the same type dealt by the weapon, and the damage can be increased only by increasing the ability modifier.
When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.
If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.
If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

A spell's components are physical requirements the spellcaster must meet to cast the spell. Each spell's description indicates whether it requires Verbal (V), Somatic (S), or Material (M) components. If the spellcaster can't provide one or more of a spell's components, the spellcaster can't cast the spell.

Verbal (V)

A Verbal component is the chanting of esoteric words that sound like nonsense to the uninitiated. The words must be uttered in a normal speaking voice. The words themselves aren't the source of the spell's power; rather, the particular combination of sounds, with specific pitch and resonance, sets the threads of magic in motion. Thus, a creature who is gagged or in an area of magical silence can't cast a spell with a Verbal component.

Somatic (S)

A Somatic component is a forceful gesticulation or an intricate set of gestures. A spellcaster must use at least one of their hands to perform these movements.

Material (M)

A Material component is a particular material used in a spell's casting, as specified in parentheses in the Components entry. These materials aren't consumed by the spell unless the spell's description states otherwise. The spellcaster must have a hand free to access them, but it can be the same hand used to perform Somatic components, if any.

If a spell doesn't consume its materials and doesn't specify a cost for them, a spellcaster can use a Component Pouch (see "Equipment") instead of providing the materials specified in the spell, or the
spellcaster can substitute a Spellcasting Focus if the caster has a feature that allows that substitution. To use a Component Pouch, you must have a hand free to reach into it, and to use a Spellcasting Focus, you must hold it unless its description says otherwise (see "Equipment" for descriptions).

A willing creature that is at least one size larger than a rider and that has an appropriate anatomy can serve as a mount, using the following rules.

Mounting and Dismounting

During your move, you can mount a creature that is within 5 feet of you or dismount. Doing so costs an amount of movement equal to half your Speed (round down). For example, if your Speed is 30 feet, you spend 15 feet of movement to mount a horse.

Controlling a Mount

You can control a mount only if it has been trained to accept a rider. Domesticated horses, mules, and similar creatures have such training.

The Initiative of a controlled mount changes to match yours when you mount it. It moves on your turn as you direct it, and it has only three action options during that turn: Dash, Disengage, and Dodge. A controlled mount can move and act even on the turn that you mount it.

In contrast, an independent mount - one that lets you ride but ignores your control - retains its place in the Initiative order and moves and acts as it likes.

Falling Off
