display.description: A sentient lawful good +1 shortsword (Int 11, Wis 13, Cha 13; hearing and sight 120 ft.; communicates by emotion) devoted to fighting evil. It always sheds bright light 15 ft. and dim light 15 ft. beyond, which only destroying it puts out. Once per dawn, its attuned wielder can cast crusader's mantle from it.

As an action, set down this 1-inch metal cube and speak its command word; it grows into a 20-ft.-square, 30-ft.-tall adamantine tower with arrow slits, a battlement, two floors joined by a ladder, and a roof trapdoor. Its door faces you, opens only at your command (a bonus action), and resists knock and similar magic. Creatures in the area make a DC 15 Dex save, taking 10d10 bludgeoning or half on success, and are pushed outside; unattended objects take the damage and are pushed. It can't be tipped over. The roof, door, and each wall have 100 HP, immunity to nonmagical non-siege weapons, and resistance to other damage; only wish repairs it, 50 HP to one part per casting. An action and the command word shrink it again, but only while it's empty.

A spongy black staff cut from a Gulthias tree; beasts within 30 ft. grow uneasy. 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dusk. It works as a magic quarterstaff, and on a hit you can spend 1 charge to heal HP equal to its damage, as blood oozes from it and you make a DC 12 Wis save or gain a short-term madness. While attuned, blights and other evil plants don't treat you as hostile unless you harm them. Breaking or burning it unleashes a scream heard 300 ft. away that kills every blight that hears it.

display.attunementNote: by a good-aligned cleric or paladin
display.description: A sunburst platinum amulet set with a large crystal, once carried by the vampire-hunting paladin Lugdana. 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn. Hold Vampires (1 charge, action): vampires and vampire spawn within 30 ft. make a DC 15 Wis save or are paralyzed 1 minute, repeating the save each turn end. Turn Undead (3 charges): when presenting it with Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, undead have disadvantage on their saves. Sunlight (5 charges, action): it sheds sunlight as bright light 30 ft. and dim light 30 ft. beyond for 10 minutes or until you end it.

A 10-lb., 12-inch silver statuette of a kneeling cleric, given to Strahd to consecrate his castle. Every creature within 30 ft. is under protection from evil and good against fiends and undead. Attuned, you can cast augury from it once per dawn without material components; use it as a holy symbol for Turn Undead or Turn the Unholy, raising the save DC by 2; and once per dawn, as an action while holding it, heal a creature you can see within 30 ft. for 3d8 + 3 HP (not undead, constructs, or fiends).
The relic of a saint who wounded Strahd; it works as a mace of disruption. If it hits a vampire or vampire spawn during a battle, it crumbles to dust when that battle ends.
A +2 shield bearing the silver dragon emblem of the Order of the Silver Dragon. It whispers warnings, giving you +2 to initiative while you aren't incapacitated.

The sentient platinum hilt of Sergei von Zarovich's crystal sword, its blade lost forever; it now works as a sun blade. Chaotic good (Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 16; hearing and sight 60 ft.; communicates by emotion). Its purpose is to destroy Strahd, out of revenge for its lost blade, and it secretly fears its own destruction.

A battleaxe carved with leaves and vines that weighs half as much as normal. It deals an extra 1d8 slashing to plants and plant creatures. In the hands of a non-good creature it sprouts thorns on each attack, dealing 1 magical piercing to the wielder afterward.

A backpack holding a bound air elemental spirit and a folded leather balloon. While worn, deploy it as an action to levitate yourself for 10 minutes without concentration, or as a reaction when falling to gain feather fall. When the spell ends, the spirit escapes and you sink gently up to 60 ft., falling if still aloft. It works again only after an hour recharging in an elemental air node.
A breath of elemental air. Inhale it and either exhale it for the effect of gust of wind, or hold it and need no air for 1 hour (ending early, as to speak, forfeits the gust).

Heavy brown iron gauntlets shaped like umber hulk claws, reaching to the elbows. Wearing both, you gain a 20-ft. burrow speed and tunnel through solid rock at 1 ft. per round. Each claw is a proficient melee weapon dealing 1d8 slashing plus Strength. While wearing them, you can't handle objects or cast spells with somatic components.

A 12-inch, 10-lb. elemental bomb made in a 1-hour ritual at an elemental node with an elemental weapon and 2,000 gp of components; the node sets its element. It detonates 1d100 hours after creation with no outward sign (identify or divination reveals when); it has AC 10, 15 HP, immunity to poison and psychic, and explodes at 0 HP. A case inscribed with the opposing element holds it safely, though removed past its time it blows 1d6 rounds later. Its effect fills a 1-mile-radius sphere, then it is spent. Air: a 1-hour windstorm; creatures ending a turn exposed make a DC 18 Con save or take 1d4 bludgeoning, light structures and weak trees fall after 10 minutes, and strong wind rules apply. Earth: earthquake (DC 18) for 1 minute. Fire: a 24-hour extreme-heat wave with a 10 percent chance each hour of a spreading wildfire that deals 3d6 fire to creatures coming within 10 ft. Water: 24 hours of heavy rain; a substantial body of water floods after 2d10 hours, rising 10 ft. and surging outward 100 ft. per round, sweeping away Large or smaller creatures and light structures.

A barnacle-studded steel trident holding a spark of Olhydra; it floats, stays cool, and water never harms it. +1 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d8 cold. While you hold it, you speak Aquan, resist cold, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on a water elemental. Once per dawn inside a water node, you can perform the Tears of Endless Anguish ritual to make a water devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you demand the largest share of spoils and part with nothing; after 24 hours attuned, barnacles grow on your skin until greater restoration (not while attuned).

A rune-etched iron war pick holding a spark of Ogrémoch, immune to rust, acid, and corrosion. +2 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d8 thunder. While you hold it, you speak Terran, resist acid, have tremorsense 60 ft., sense (but can't pinpoint) precious metals and stones within 60 ft., and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on an earth elemental. 3 charges, regaining 1d3 at dawn: spend 1 as an action to cast 2nd-level shatter (DC 17). Once per dawn inside an earth node, you can perform the Rumbling ritual to make an earth devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you love to break things and cause ruin.

An open-faced steel dwarven helm ringed by a gold circlet with seven spikes. While worn, you resist psychic damage and have advantage on saves against being charmed. 3 charges, regaining 1d3 at dawn: as a bonus action, spend 1 to inspire a creature within 60 ft. that can see or hear you, which can add a d6 to one ability check, attack roll, or save before the end of your next turn.

display.attunementNote: by a good-aligned dwarf, fighter, or paladin
display.description: King Torhild Flametongue's battered greataxe, its rune for orc split in two. While you hold it: +2 to attack and damage; a natural 20 against an orc forces a DC 17 Con save or it drops to 0 HP; orcs can't surprise you while you aren't incapacitated, and you sense orcs within 120 ft. not behind total cover (not where); and you and friends within 30 ft. can't be frightened while you aren't incapacitated. Sentient lawful good (Int 6, Wis 15, Cha 10; sight and hearing 120 ft. with darkvision), it speaks through emotion and the odd verse of old Dwarvish. Grim and unbending, it scorns cowardice and deceit, exists to defend dwarves, and urges you against giants, goblins, and above all orcs.

A dart etched with wind spirals. Whisper 'seek' and throw it at a creature within 120 ft. that you've seen before (sight not needed now); with a clear path, winds carry it instantly through 1-inch gaps and around corners. The target makes a DC 16 Dex save or takes 1d4 piercing and 3d4 lightning. Then, or if there's no path, it becomes an ordinary dart.

A griffon-bone boomerang marked with the air sigil; a thrown ranged weapon (60/120 ft.) usable by anyone proficient with javelins. A hit deals 1d4 bludgeoning and 3d4 thunder, and the target makes a DC 10 Con save or is stunned until the end of its next turn; a miss returns it to your hand. After dealing thunder once, it loses the thunder and stun until it spends an hour in an elemental air node.

A keen flint dagger holding a spark of Imix; it throws sparks on solid hits, stays warm, and smolders 1d4 minutes after drawing blood. +2 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 2d6 fire. While you hold it, you speak Ignan, resist fire, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on a fire elemental. Once per dawn inside a fire node, you can perform the Dance of the All-Consuming Fire ritual to make a fire devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you act without thinking and take reckless risks.

A ten-gallon glass-and-bronze tank on a leather harness, holding a water weird. While wearing it, open it as an action to release the weird, which acts right after you, stays bound to the tank, and obeys your telepathic commands (no action). You can close it as an action only after the weird retracts or dies. If the weird dies, the tank works again only after 24 hours in an elemental water node, which forms a new weird. The tank has AC 15, 50 HP, vulnerability to bludgeoning, and immunity to poison and psychic; destroying it kills the weird.

A silver spear set with dark sapphires, light as a breeze, holding a spark of Yan-C-Bin. +2 to attack and damage, it has the finesse property, and hits deal an extra 1d6 lightning. While you hold it, you speak Auran, resist lightning, and once per dawn can cast dominate monster (DC 17) on an air elemental. Once per dawn inside an air node, you can perform the Song of the Four Winds ritual to make an air devastation orb. Flaw while attuned: you break vows and plans, caring nothing for duty or honor.

A snug, air-embroidered suit with gliding flaps. 3 charges: as a bonus action, spend 1 to gain a 30-ft. fly speed until you land. You lose 5 ft. of altitude at the end of each turn, or drop to the ground at once if you didn't fly 30 ft. horizontally that turn; landing ends it. It recharges fully after an hour in an elemental air node.

A 10-ft.-wide floating leaf vehicle whose tendrils carry it over land, across water (not under it), and through the air at walk, fly, and swim speeds of 20 ft., with hover, following your spoken directions while you ride. It carries 300 lb. freely, or up to double that at half speed.

A magic rose in one of five colors, each tied to a damage type (acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison) and showing a harmless visual effect when held. Held by the stem, it gives you resistance to its type; if a single source would still deal you more than 10 of that type, the rose disintegrates and you take none. As an action, blow its petals into a 20-ft. cone of its element: DC 15 Con save, 3d10 of that type, half on success, destroying the rose.

One packet of ground rust monster antennae. As an action, throw it to fill a 10-ft. cube from you: nonmagical ferrous metal there rusts instantly to useless dust, and creatures made wholly or partly of ferrous metal make a DC 13 Con save, 4d8 necrotic, half on success.

A +1 quarterstaff with 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn; spending the last, roll a d20, and on a 1 it bursts harmlessly and is destroyed. On a melee hit you can spend up to 3 charges for an extra 1d8 lightning each. When you take damage while holding it, use your reaction and 3 charges to turn invisible and teleport with your gear up to 60 ft. to a space you can see, staying invisible until your next turn starts or you attack, cast a spell, or deal damage.

An 80-lb., 100-gallon cauldron on eight clawed feet that only Iggwilv or Baba Yaga can switch (with an action and a touch) between a gold form, embossed with bare trees, leaves, and brooms, and an iron form, embossed with eight each of bats, toads, cats, lizards, and snakes. A humanoid attuning makes a DC 15 Con save or is aged to frailty (half speed, sight and hearing limited to 30 ft., disadvantage on checks, attacks, and saves, and death of old age in 3d8 days), reversible only by wish or divine intervention; a hag coven of three can attune together until it disbands. It has one minor beneficial and one minor detrimental random property. Gold: stirred water becomes hot stew feeding four per gallon; once per dawn, wine stirred 10 minutes becomes an elixir giving four per gallon 10 temporary HP (vanishing after an hour); filled with 90 gallons of water and 10 of wine, it focuses a scrying that the target automatically fails, even across planes, consuming the liquid; once per dawn, a broom dipped in it becomes a broom of flying for 3 days. Iron: once per dawn, scream into it as an action to release an obedient swarm of bats for 1 minute, acting after you; once per dawn, a gallon or more of blood stirred 1 minute puts humanoids within 100 ft. per gallon to sleep for 1 hour (not attuned or charm-immune creatures), waking on damage or a shake; once per 8 days, a branch tipped with a dead frog or toad and dipped in water becomes a wand of polymorph with 3 charges that crumbles when emptied; touching it with a unicorn horn for 1 minute while reciting the poem The Witch Queen's Cauldron freezes every unattuned creature within 1,000 ft. in time (helpless, unaware, untouchable, and unaffected by magic) until the ritual is repeated, the cauldron is destroyed or leaves the plane, or a frozen creature meets an antimagic field or a unicorn horn. It is a Medium object (AC 19, 80 HP) harmed only by a flame tongue or frost brand; at 0 HP it shatters into eight pieces, ending its effects and stripping every hag coven in the multiverse of Shared Spellcasting until a wish reassembles the pieces within 5 ft. of one another.

An 8-ft.-long, 25-lb. flying contraption with a 14-ft. wingspan. It carries a rider of up to 300 lb. (with gear) at a fly speed of 30 ft. by spoken directions, but can't hover. If it loses its rider while aloft, it falls and can't fly again for 1d6 + 4 days.

One packet. As an action, sprinkle it on yourself or a creature you can see within 5 ft. to grant a 30-ft. fly speed with hover for 1 minute; if aloft when it ends, the creature floats safely to the ground.
A sparkling golden mist that pours like water. After drinking it, you have advantage on one ability check, attack roll, or save of your choice within the next hour.

display.attunementNote: by a fey or a spellcaster
display.description: Iron shears. Once per dawn, as an action, snip away the shadow of a humanoid you can see within 5 ft. (an unwilling target keeps it with a DC 15 Cha save). The shadow stays rooted until you use a bonus action, while you can see it, either to steer it up to 30 ft. across any solid or liquid surface (harmless, unharmable, invisible in darkness, silent, needing nothing) or to release it, after which it acts on its own as a fey shadow whose Strength Drain knocks creatures unconscious at 0 Strength rather than killing them (recovering after a rest). A shadowless creature is cursed until a curse-ending spell or the shadow's destruction returns its shadow.

A +3 vorpal greatsword that ignores resistance to slashing. On a natural 20 against a creature with a head, it lops one off, killing it if it can't live without it; creatures immune to slashing, headless, with legendary actions, or too big instead take an extra 6d8 slashing. While attuned you're proficient with greatswords and can use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls. Sentient chaotic good (Int 9, Wis 14, Cha 18; hearing and darkvision 120 ft.; speaks, reads, and understands Common in a silvery voice), it craves slaying evil dragons. Fickle, it ends attunement after you miss three times in a row; after each long rest you can win it back with a contested Charisma check, and in no other way.

A +2 longsword. Once per dawn, as an action, cast revivify from it by touching the target with the blade. Sentient lawful good (Int 8, Wis 11, Cha 15; sight and hearing 60 ft.; speaks, reads, and understands Common and Draconic), it frets over your welfare and hates backing down from a fight.

display.attunementNote: by Mister Light or his chosen successor
display.description: A 3-lb. rod set with red glass and topped with butterfly wings. Attuned, it is a +3 mace dealing an extra 1d8 radiant. Within the Witchlight Carnival it senses the mood of every creature of Int 4 or higher; as an action you can pinpoint the happiest, and its wings turn clockwise when spirits are high and counterclockwise when they're low. Sentient chaotic good (Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 14; sight and hearing 30 ft.; communicates by emotion), it wants everyone at the carnival enjoying themselves. Its holder is vulnerable to lightning; its attuned bearer can't be blinded, deafened, petrified, or stunned and can cast dancing lights, polymorph, or ray of frost as an action without components using Charisma (after each polymorph roll a d8; on a 3 or 8, no more polymorph until dawn).

display.attunementNote: by Mister Witch or his chosen successor
display.description: A glowing gold pocket watch on a chain, ticking only for its holder, whose face shows the carnival ringed by a tiny henge whose moving shadows mark the time. As an action, its attuned owner can start packing up or setting up the whole Witchlight Carnival on the same plane; over 1 hour every carnival object moves itself into place, creatures are unaffected, the process can't be stopped, and the property is then unusable for 8 hours. The attuned bearer can cast fire bolt, invisibility, or message as an action without components using Intelligence (after each invisibility roll a d8; on a 3 or 8, no more invisibility until dawn), gains 30 lb. while attuned, and must eat and drink eight times the normal amount each day.
A +1 greataxe that deals an extra 2d6 slashing on hits against plants, plant creatures, and unattended wooden objects.
A 1-lb. sphere of thick, cracked glass. Within 60 ft. of it, speak its command word to make it shed light as the light spell.

While worn, your Constitution is 20 (no effect if already 20 or higher). After a successful unarmed strike, you can deal an extra 2d10 force and either regain HP equal to that force damage or gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or save before the end of your next turn.

A rusty 3-inch, 1-lb. iron ball. Once per dawn, as an action, speak its command word and hurl it at a Huge or smaller creature you can see within 60 ft., making a ranged attack with Dex plus proficiency. On a hit, it unfolds into bands that restrain the target until you speak the word again as a bonus action; a miss or release returns it to a ball. Any creature can use an action and a DC 20 Strength check to snap the bands, destroying them; a failure bars that creature from trying again for 24 hours.

A scroll that isn't used up. After 30 days of study (8 hours a day), make a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check; failure deals 16d10 psychic and requires another 30 days before retrying. On success your Intelligence rises by 2 (max 22, once only), you gain advantage on saves against spells and magical effects, and a stone golem appears within 60 ft. as your ally, crumbling to dust if you die.

A gray figurine of Orcus carved from an ogre's petrified heart, reeking of rot within 5 ft. It is a Tiny object (AC 17, 3 HP) immune to all damage but radiant, and detect evil and good reveals it as desecrated. While intact: undead within 30 ft. can't be turned, and dead creatures within 30 ft. can't be revived. Praying to Orcus while holding it for at least an hour has a 10 percent chance to summon a smoky avatar (wraith stats, chaotic evil) that attacks every non-undead it meets and vanishes after 1 hour or at 0 HP; once summoned, it can't be called again for 30 days.

A golden hand mirror that serves as a wand. While held, +1 to spell attack rolls, and your spell attacks ignore half cover. It sheds dim light 5 ft. when surrounded by darkness. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, cast enhance ability on yourself only.
Shimmering scale mail. You add your full Dexterity modifier to AC instead of a maximum of +2, and it imposes no disadvantage on Stealth.
A single-edged magic sword carved from a giant serpent's fang, its hilt reshaping to fit any hand. Hits deal an extra 1d10 poison.

A clear crystal +3 quarterstaff with 6 charges. As a bonus action, spend 1 to give yourself or a creature you can see a d4 to add to one ability check, attack roll, damage roll, or save before your next turn starts (lost if unused). Spending the last charge, roll a d20: on 9 or lower it becomes a plain quarterstaff that shatters on its first damaging hit; on 10 or higher it regains 1d6 charges.
While worn, cast telekinesis at will, targeting only unattended objects. Its attuned wearer commands Stonky's constructs, though skitterwidgets ignore commands spoken from more than 30 ft. away.
While worn: +1 AC, awareness of your surroundings even while asleep, and advantage on sight-based Perception. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, cast see invisibility from it.

A hell-forged infernal iron banner bearing a small sealed cage with an incapacitated quasit inside (cage AC 19, 10 HP, immune to all but force). If the quasit dies or escapes, it vanishes in smoke and a new one appears while the cage is intact. While you hold it, your weapon attacks and those of allies within 300 ft. count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity.

Works as a vorpal sword, with 2 minor beneficial, 1 major beneficial, and 1 major detrimental random property (the last suppressed while an archdevil is attuned). Ruler of Avernus: as an action, point it at a devil you can see within 60 ft., which makes a DC 22 Cha save or is charmed for 1 hour and obeys you; ordering it toward what it sees as suicide ends the charm and the sword can't target that devil again. Infernal Recall: as an action, cast word of recall, delivering creatures within 30 ft. of the current ruler of Avernus, or to a sanctuary you choose if you rule it. Destroyed by casting it into the River Styx or melting it in the forge that made it.

display.attunementNote: by an evil cleric or paladin
display.description: Arkhan the Cruel's battleaxe. +3 to attack and damage; on a natural 20 against a creature, it takes an extra 2d8 necrotic and you regain that much HP.

Steel gauntlets. Wearing both, any nonmagical weapon you hold in them counts as magical. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, wreathe one or two held melee weapons in flame, each dealing an extra 1d6 fire on hits until you sheathe or let go of either.
A weapon of infernal iron veined with hellfire that sheds dim light 5 ft. A humanoid killed by it has its soul drawn into the River Styx, where it is instantly reborn as a lemure.

display.attunementNote: by a creature that speaks Infernal
display.description: A bulky, eyeless pit fiend helm that resizes to fit; you see through it normally. You know the location and kind of every devil within 1,000 ft. and can speak telepathically to one or broadcast to all (they can't reply). 3 charges, all returning 24 hours after the last is spent: as an action, spend 1 to cast dominate monster (DC 21) on a devil only (a non-devil target wastes the charge), and a devil that sees you knows you tried. A non-devil using this in the Nine Hells has a 20 percent chance of drawing a narzugon on a nightmare within 1d4 hours, intent on reclaiming the helm for its master.

A 3-lb., 5- to 6-inch airtight cube of infernal iron, bone, or horn used to hold diabolic contracts. An object placed inside is sealed in; no magic can open the box, and it becomes immune to damage. Each opens by its own mundane trick, which a creature that knows it can perform as an action. Studying it for an hour allows a DC 30 Intelligence (Investigation) check to learn the trick; failing by 5 or more forces a DC 18 Wis save, 42 (12d6) psychic, half on success.

A narzugon's full nightmare harness: bridle, bit, reins, saddle, stirrups, and spurs. A nightmare wearing it serves the spur-wearer until that wearer dies or the tack is removed. As an action, clash the spurs or scrape them through blood to call it; it arrives within 20 ft. at the start of your next turn, acts on your initiative as your ally, and stays 1 day, until either of you dies, or until you dismiss it as an action. If it dies, it re-forms in the Nine Hells in 24 hours and can be called again. A nightmare must first be subdued to be harnessed.

The Frost Father, forged by the frost giant god Thrym and favored by Kostchtchie; icy and wreathed in mist. While you hold it you are immune to cold, and whenever it damages a creature, it releases a 30-ft.-radius burst dealing 10 (3d6) cold to each creature there.
Plate armor granting +2 AC, resistance to poison, and advantage on checks and saves to avoid or escape being grappled.

A celestial shield, now twisted into a shifting fiendish face, that imprisons the pit fiend Gargauth. While holding it you gain +2 AC and resistance to fire. While Gargauth is inside it is sentient (Int 22, Wis 18, Cha 24; hearing and truesight 120 ft.; speaks Common and Infernal in a hollow whisper; telepathic within 120 ft.). 3 charges, regaining all at dawn: as an action spend 1 for fireball or 2 for wall of fire lasting 1 minute without concentration (DC 21). Once per dawn, on its own choice during your turn, it radiates dread for 1 minute: hostile creatures starting their turn within 20 ft. make a DC 18 Wis save or are frightened until their next turn, immune for 24 hours on success. Calling itself the Hidden Lord, Gargauth hints it is a trapped angel, steers its bearer toward cruelty and domination, and wrongly believes it can escape in the Nine Hells. Dispel evil and good has a 1 percent chance to free it (certain if cast by a solar, planetar, or archdevil), or a god can free it by touch and name.

A magical explosive for firearms, kept in waterproof packets (five shots) or airtight kegs (five hundred). Set alight, dropped, or handled roughly, it explodes, dealing fire to everything within 20 ft.: 1d6 for a packet, 9d6 for a keg, halved with a DC 12 Dex save. Dispel magic renders it permanently inert.

A 5-inch, third-of-a-pound infernal iron coin inscribed in Infernal that binds one soul, which you can feel raging or despairing. Evil creatures can carry any number; a non-evil creature carrying more than its Constitution modifier has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saves. 3 charges: as an action, spend 1 to drain 1d10 temporary HP from the soul, or to ask it a question it must answer truthfully in a sentence or two from what it knew in life. A curse-removing spell or spending the last charge frees the soul and rusts the coin away, as does destroying it (AC 19, 1 HP per remaining charge, harmed only by a hellfire weapon or an infernal war machine's furnace). Freed souls go to their god's realm or alignment plane; lawful evil ones usually rise from the Styx as lemures. Freeing a soul is a good act. They are the currency of the Nine Hells, minted by Mammon on Minauros.

display.attunementNote: by a creature the sword deems worthy
display.description: The fallen Zariel's celestial-steel longsword, glowing faintly and humming; it seeks a brave, heroic wielder and allows attunement immediately. Your first attunement permanently transforms you into an idealized, heavenly self (no magic reverses it): your alignment becomes lawful good, you speak, read, and write Celestial, resist necrotic and radiant, your Charisma becomes 20 (if lower), you grow feathered wings (fly 90 ft., hover), you gain truesight 60 ft., and you take new personality traits rolled on its tables. It sheds bright light 5 ft. and dim light 5 ft. beyond (15 and 15 as a bonus action, or back); fiends have disadvantage on attacks within its bright light. It has 2 minor beneficial random properties and deals an extra 9 (2d8) radiant, or 16 (3d10) two-handed, and an evil creature damaged by it makes a DC 17 Con save or is blinded until the end of its next turn. Sentient lawful good (Int 10, Wis 20, Cha 18; sight and hearing 30 ft.; communicates by emotion); while held, advantage on Insight checks. Zariel can destroy it by grasping it, and it is destroyed if used to shatter the Companion unless wielded by an angel of CR 15+ or a good cleric or paladin of 10th level or higher; if Zariel dies in the Nine Hells, it becomes as breakable as any longsword.

A glossy ebony mask with horns and a skull-like look that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to acid (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, acid damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against black dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You can also breathe underwater.

A glossy azure mask ringed with spikes and crowned by a ridged horn that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to lightning (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, lightning damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against blue dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. Creatures you deal lightning damage to can't take reactions until their next turn.

A mottled green mask with a frilled crest and spiked jaw plates that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to poison (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, poison damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against green dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You can also breathe underwater.

A glossy crimson mask with swept-back horns and spiked cheek ridges that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to fire (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, fire damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against red dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. Creatures and flammable objects you deal fire damage to catch fire, taking 1d6 fire at the start of each of their turns until someone in reach uses an action to put it out.

A gleaming white mask touched with pale blue under a spined crest that reshapes to fit its wearer. While worn and attuned: resistance to cold (immunity if you already resist it; if already immune, cold damage instead heals you for half of it); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon that needs a rest to recharge gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft. if you have it) and, once per day, blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak and understand Draconic and have advantage on Charisma checks against white dragons; and once per day you can turn a failed save into a success. While at half your HP maximum or lower, your melee attacks deal an extra 1d8 cold.

The horn of Ephelomon, Tiamat's ancient red dragon consort, given to dragons for their war on the giants. So huge that two Medium creatures (or one Large or bigger) must hold it while a third sounds it, it makes the ground thrum; its low drone unsettles animals for miles and warns every dragon within 2,000 miles of great danger. Coded blasts once sent specific messages. Made to warn chromatic dragons, it is now misused by the Cult of the Dragon to summon them to the Well of Dragons.
A spear holding 10 charges of daylight, meant for dim forest undergrowth, triggered by the Draconic command phrase 'Tiamat's eyes shine' inscribed on its crossguard.

A dagger made from a dragon's fang with a leather-wrapped root for a handle and no crossguard. +1 to attack and damage, and hits deal an extra 1d6 acid; against enemies of the Cult of the Dragon the bonus becomes +2 and the acid 2d6.

A sentient neutral evil greatsword that speaks Common and Netherese. Unattuned, it gives +1 to attack and damage and deals an extra 1d6 necrotic on hits. Attuned, the bonus is +2 and the necrotic 2d6, and a creature you hit can't regain HP for 1 minute, ending early on a DC 15 Con save at the end of each of its turns. Attuned and in hand, use an action to spend charges (4, regaining 1d4 at midnight) to cast detect magic (1), detect evil and good (1), or detect thoughts (2).
A jeweled Cult of the Dragon insignia that flares purple as combat begins. While worn, your unarmed strikes and natural weapons gain +1 to attack and damage rolls and count as magical.

Bringing two or more dragon masks together fuses them into this crown of five roaring chromatic heads over a new draconic mask covering face, neck, and shoulders. While worn and attuned: resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, and poison (each becoming immunity if you already resist it, or healing you for half the damage if already immune); unarmored, add your Charisma bonus to AC; a breath weapon needing a rest gains recharge 6; darkvision 60 ft. (or +60 ft.) and once per day blindsight 30 ft. for 5 minutes; you speak Draconic; and five times per day you can turn a failed save into a success. You also gain the color-specific benefits of one mask of your choice, including advantage on Charisma checks against dragons of that color: Dragon Fire (red), Lingering Shock (blue), Water Breathing (black or green), or Winter's Fury (white).
A golden stein decorated with dancing dwarves and grain. 3 charges, regaining all at dawn: grasp the handle and say 'Illefarn' to spend 1 and fill it with three pints of rich dwarven ale.

An icicle-like wand with 7 charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn; spending the last, roll a d20, and on a 20 it melts away. As an action, cast from it even if you can't cast spells, with no components: ray of frost (free, or 1 charge at 5th level; +5 to hit), sleet storm (3 charges, DC 15), or ice storm (4 charges, DC 15).

Lightweight bronze bracers lined with purple velvet. While wearing them, all your speeds increase by 10 feet, and you have advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the paralyzed or restrained condition on yourself.

A grayish-purple cape with silver runes along its hem. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a bonus action, expend 1 charge to enlarge yourself for 10 minutes (or until you dismiss it as a bonus action): your size increases by one category (or as large as the space allows), you have advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and your weapon and unarmed strike hits add your proficiency bonus to damage.

You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. Made for Tergon, a human hero of old Neverwinter, this breastplate bears a gold dragon motif and grants advantage on saving throws against the breath weapons of dragons.

Carvings of decapitated mind flayers adorn the blade. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this greataxe. An aberration hit with it takes an extra 1d12 slashing damage, and if it is grappling a creature it must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or release each creature it is grappling.
A +1 battleaxe that deals maximum damage when its wielder attacks a plant creature or an object made of wood. Its creator used it for protection in the forest while cutting firewood.
A +1 mace made for a cleric of Lathander, its solid brass head shaped like a sunburst. On command it glows as bright as a torch, and while glowing it deals an extra 1d6 radiant damage to undead.

The haft is inlaid with crushed pearlescent stones that give it a faint glow. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this war pick. As a bonus action you can cast daylight centered on a point on the pick; this can't be used again until the next dawn.

A gemstone holding a single-use spell modification. When you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action while holding it, you can modify the spell as described below; only one mind crystal per spell, and not alongside a Metamagic option. Afterward it becomes a nonmagical gem worth 50 gp.
Careful (Uncommon): up to three creatures affected by the spell automatically succeed on their saves against it.
Distant (Uncommon): a spell with a range of 5 feet or more (not self) gains 100 feet of range; a touch spell gets a range of 30 feet.
Empowered (Uncommon): reroll up to three damage dice, using the new rolls.
Extended (Uncommon): a spell lasting 1 minute or longer has its duration doubled, to a maximum of 24 hours.
Heightened (Rare): one creature affected by the spell has disadvantage on its first save against it.
Quickened (Rare): the casting time becomes 1 bonus action.
Subtle (Common): cast the spell without verbal or somatic components.

A soft violet cap stitched with the folds of a brain. As a bonus action while wearing it, project psychic energy in a 60-foot cone: each creature there makes a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw, taking 5d8 psychic damage and becoming stunned for 1 minute on a failure (repeating the save at the end of each of its turns), or half damage only on a success. Once used, this can't be used again until the next dawn.
While you wear this adamantine crown, you have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws, and resistance to psychic damage.

As an action, place this 1-inch granite sphere on the ground and speak its Terran command word ("petrification") to make it grow into a tower 20 feet on a side and 30 feet high, with arrow slits, a battlement, two floors joined by a ladder, and a roof trapdoor. Speak the word again while touching it to shrink it back; it must be empty. Muddy knobs constantly extrude and retract across its surface.
Each creature in the area where it appears makes a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10d10 bludgeoning damage on a failure or half on a success, and is pushed to an unoccupied space next to the tower; unworn objects take the damage and are pushed automatically. When it expands it merges with any natural stone it touches.
Its small door faces you and opens only at your command (a bonus action), and is immune to knock and similar magic. The tower is adamantine and can't be tipped over. The roof, door, and each wall have 100 hit points, immunity to damage from nonmagical weapons other than siege weapons, and resistance to all other damage; while merged with natural stone it is immune to all damage. Only a wish spell can repair it, restoring 50 hit points to the roof, door, or one wall per casting.

Made from a single piece of mystical green glass stronger than steel. You gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws while wearing it, plus a +4 bonus to saving throws or checks to avoid dropping or being disarmed of anything held in that hand.
When you drink this black potion swirling with pink and purple flecks, you have advantage for 1 hour on saving throws to avoid or end the charmed or stunned condition on yourself.

This ring has 6 charges and regains 1d6 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, expend 1 charge to project your voice clearly to all creatures within 1 mile for 1 minute, regardless of noise; magical silence, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood blocks it. Creatures you can see understand you even if they don't know the language you speak.

display.attunementNote: by a bard, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
display.description:
The top of this magic quarterstaff is shaped like a spider, and it deals an extra 1d6 poison damage on a hit when used to make a weapon attack.
Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast spider climb (1 charge) or web (2 charges; save DC 15). If you expend the last charge, roll a d20; on a 1, the staff crumbles to dust.

display.attunementNote: by a bard, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
display.description:
This slender, hollow 3-pound staff is made of glass yet is as strong as oak. While holding it, you have a +1 bonus to AC.
Spells. The staff has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can expend charges to cast mage armor (1 charge) or shield (2 charges). If you expend the last charge, roll a d20; on a 1, the staff shatters.

A gold statuette of an elf worth 100 gp. A non-evil creature grasping it can ask a question and receive a telepathic answer as though it had cast augury. Each creature can activate it only once, ever.

This silver chime is engraved with delicate sigils. While holding it, you can use an action to cast banishment (save DC 20); a target with 50 hit points or fewer automatically fails its save. Once used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Burnished, entwined metal rods form this crown, which the Dark Powers of the Domain of Dread gave to Kas so he would deliver Vecna to them. To attune, place it on your head and speak a true desire of your heart.
Random Properties. 1 minor beneficial, 1 major beneficial, and 1 minor detrimental property.
Perfect Disguise. As an action, transform to look and feel exactly like any creature you've seen at least once that is no more than one size smaller or larger than you, voice included. Your size and speed become the creature's; you otherwise keep your statistics, and the crown melds into you undetectably. The form lasts until you die, your attunement ends, or you use another action to change form. Interactions reveal no illusion, and you count as that creature for spells, traps, and defenses. Your lies always seem true to any magical or mundane detection, you receive sending spells meant for you or the disguised creature, and scrying aimed at that creature targets you. Only a wish spell reveals your true nature. In your true form, you can make the crown visible or not.
Destroying the Crown. If its wearer is killed by the creature it is disguised as, the crown disintegrates.

The Wind Dukes of Aaqa wove their power into the Rod of Law to imprison the demon lord Miska the Wolf-Spider on Pandemonium; the rod shattered into seven pieces scattered across the multiverse.
Possessing the Broken Rod. It can't be attuned while broken. Holding a piece, you know the general location of the next consecutive piece. Pieces can be assembled or disassembled as an action, but a partial rod gains no other abilities. Each piece can cast its associated spell from the Rod Pieces table as an action, once per dawn.
Possessing the Whole Rod. Once all seven are reassembled, it can be attuned. It is a +3 quarterstaff. It has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 daily at dawn: as an action, expend 1 charge to cast any spell from the Rod Pieces table, or cast detect evil and good at no cost. A non-lawful wielder finds their worldview shifting toward keeping a personal code.
Destroying the Rod. The assembled rod must be immersed in lava in the Abyss for fifty years. A single piece destroyed this way re-forms after one year and teleports to a random place in the multiverse.

A colorful hammock woven with traditional Ataguan designs, usable only by a member of the Green Doctors. As an action, unfold it on a solid surface to open a two-way portal to the Ghost Orchid Tepui in the Feywild or to the Drought Elder in the Far Realm (your choice). Folding it up as an action closes the portal. Once it has opened a portal, it can't do so again for 1d8 hours.

An intelligent battleaxe forged by the archwizard Ahghairon to defend Waterdeep: a rune-etched steel handle wrapped in blue dragon hide with a star sapphire pommel, its silver, electrum, and steel head shimmering deep blue.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with it, and the shield spell offers no defense against it. A fiend or undead you hit takes an extra 2d6 radiant damage.
Hurling. It has 3 charges, regained daily at dawn. Expend 1 to throw it (range 60/180); hit or miss, it returns to your hand or feet at the end of the turn.
Illumination. As an action, make it glow blue (bright light 30 feet, dim light 30 more) or quench the glow.
Sentience. Lawful neutral, Int 12, Wis 15, Cha 15, with hearing and darkvision 120 feet. It speaks, reads, and understands Common, communicates telepathically with its wielder in a calm, delicate voice, and senses non-lawful creatures within 120 feet.
Personality. Sworn to protect Waterdeep, it patiently seeks a law-abiding wielder devoted to the city. If used against its will, it can become ten times heavier and adhere to any Medium or larger object or surface; only a wish spell can separate them without destroying one, though the axe can end this at any time.

display.attunementNote: by someone designated by the Open Lord of Waterdeep
display.description: This badge marks a captain of Waterdeep's City Watch and bears the city's emblem. While wearing it, you gain a +2 bonus to AC if you aren't using a shield. If it is more than 5 feet from you for over 1 minute, it vanishes and reappears within 5 feet of the Open Lord. While holding it, the Open Lord knows your location on the same plane while you remain attuned, and can end your attunement by touching it as an action.

display.attunementNote: by a Blackstaff heir, who must be a wizard
display.description:
The sentient, rune-carved symbol of office of the Blackstaff, Waterdeep's highest-ranking wizard. It has all the properties of a staff of power, plus the following.
Animate Walking Statues. Within the city, expend charges as an action to animate or deactivate one walking statue of Waterdeep per charge. Animated statues obey the telepathic commands of Khelben Arunsun's spirit within the staff, and go inanimate if deactivated or if the staff is broken.
Dispel Magic. Expend 1 charge as a bonus action to cast dispel magic on a creature, object, or effect you touch with the staff; against an unwilling creature or its possession, you must first hit it with a melee attack using the staff.
Drain Magic. When you hit a creature that uses spell slots with the staff, expend 1 charge as a bonus action to make it expend its highest-level slot.
Master of Enchantment. When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher while holding it, an Arcana check (DC 10 + spell level) lets you cast it without expending a slot.
Sentience. Neutral, Int 22, Wis 15, Cha 18, hearing and darkvision 120 feet, telepathy with its holder.
Personality. It holds the spirits of every previous Blackstaff, dominated by its devious creator Khelben. It protects Waterdeep and its Open Lord first and empowers its wielder second, and stops functioning for a Blackstaff who no longer serves its wishes until it finds a worthy heir.
Spirit Trap. A Blackstaff who dies is trapped in the staff and can't be raised. Destroying the staff frees the spirits, but Khelben can lodge in any remaining piece, which keeps Sentience and can remake the staff at will, trapping the spirits again.

This armband appears to have thin daggers strapped to it. As an action, pull up to two magic daggers from it and hurl them immediately, making a ranged attack with each. A dagger not hurled at once vanishes, and they vanish after they hit or miss. It never runs out.

While holding it, you have advantage on saving throws against the spells and breath weapons of dragons and the breath weapons of other dragon-type creatures. A dragon you touch with it can move through Waterdeep ignoring Ahghairon's dragonward until touched again or until a time you proclaim. It has 10 charges and regains 1d10 daily at dawn: expend 1 as an action to cast command, and a dragon targeted has disadvantage on the save.

Speak the command word as an action and throw this bright plume into a Large unoccupied space on the ground within 5 feet, and it becomes a living diatryma (an axe beak whose beak deals piercing damage) for up to 6 hours. It reverts early at 0 hit points or when you touch it and speak the word again as an action, and then can't be used for 7 days. It is friendly, can be ridden, understands your languages, and obeys your spoken commands, defending itself if given none.

While wearing this eye patch, you have advantage on sight-based Perception checks, are unaffected by Sunlight Sensitivity, and are immune to magic that reads your thoughts or determines whether you are lying. Creatures can communicate telepathically with you only if you allow it.

display.attunementNote: by a creature with a humanoid build
display.description:
Worn by the Masked Lords of Waterdeep to make each indistinguishable from the others. The helm, amulet, and robe function as a single item, attuned together, but only within Waterdeep and its sewers.
Lord's Helm. A face-concealing bucket helm with eye screens. Your voice sounds genderless, and you are immune to magic that reads your thoughts, determines whether you are lying, or reveals your alignment or creature type. Telepathy reaches you only if you allow it.
Lord's Amulet. Bears the crest of Waterdeep and functions as an amulet of proof against detection and location.
Lord's Robe. Functions as a ring of free action and makes you appear a nondescript, androgynous humanoid 6 feet tall.

Write a message of fifty words or fewer on this parchment and speak a creature's name, and it folds into a Tiny paper bird that flies to that recipient (turning to ash if they are on another plane). The bird is an object with 1 hit point, AC 13, flying speed 60 feet, Dex 16, 1 in all other abilities, and immunity to poison and psychic damage. It flies directly to within 5 feet of the recipient and becomes ordinary parchment that only they can unfold. It turns to ash if its hit points or speed drop to 0 or it is immobilized. Usually sold in boxes of 1d6 + 3 sheets.
While wearing this ring, you have advantage on Insight checks to determine whether someone is lying to you.

A glossy greenish-gray palm-sized stone that is actually the aboleth Golorr, transformed into an object.
Random Properties. 1 minor beneficial and 1 minor detrimental property.
Legend Lore. It has 3 charges and regains 1d3 daily at dawn; expend 1 to cast legend lore, speaking directly with the aboleth, which can't lie but is often cryptic. It knows where Lord Neverember's secret vault lies, that three keys open it, and that the gold dragon Aurinax guards it.
Failed Memory. When your attunement ends, make a DC 16 Wisdom save or lose all memory of the stone and what it taught you. Remove curse has a 20 percent chance to restore it; greater restoration always does.
Sentience. Lawful evil, Int 18, Wis 15, Cha 18, hearing and darkvision 120 feet, telepathy with its attuned owner, and it learns the greatest desires of any creature communicating with it. It hungers for information, demands to be passed on often, and tries to take control of an owner who refuses.
Personality. Alien, domineering, and hungry for knowledge, it thinks itself an ageless god.
Destroying the Stone. It is immune to all damage and isn't a creature. Antipathy/sympathy cast on it, choosing antipathy against aberrations, turns it to mucus and releases Golorr within 30 feet, enraged and attacking all creatures it sees.

This armor appears as a pot of bubbling black ichor. When you attune to it, the ichor contours to your skin and the pot vanishes; it can be worn under clothes and doesn't impede bodily functions. It can't be removed unless you choose to or die, at which point the ichor flows back into the reappearing pot. While wearing it, you have resistance to poison damage, and it doesn't impose disadvantage on Stealth checks.
As an action, blow this horn to cast arms of Hadar, fog cloud, gust of wind, or web from it (save DC 13). Each spell can't be cast from it again until the next dawn.

Seven syrupy bands of brightly colored liquid. When you drink it, you and your gear take on a rainbow-hued appearance for 1 hour, during which you can use a bonus action to turn any colors you choose. Mimicking your surroundings makes your hues shift to match them, granting advantage on Stealth checks until you change colors or the potion ends.

A magic boat 10 feet wide and 30 feet long with four legs, giving it a walking and swimming speed of 20 feet (it can't go underwater). It moves at your spoken direction while you ride it, and creatures of your choice aboard gain a +1 bonus to AC. It carries 1,000 pounds without hindrance, or up to twice that at half speed.

A foul manuscript, most believe authored by Vecna, cataloging every vile idea and black magic he could find, with later additions stitched in by other evil writers. Plants wither near it, animals shun it, and even stone it rests on long enough crumbles.
An attuned creature must spend 80 hours studying it to gain its benefits and can then add evil lore to it. A non-evil creature that attunes makes a DC 17 Charisma save or becomes neutral evil. The book vanishes if you go 10 days without an evil act or willingly do good. If you die while attuned, a great evil claims your soul and you can't be restored to life while it is held.
Circle of Death. As an action, cast circle of death (DC 20); afterward roll a d6, and on 1-5 this can't be used again until dawn.
Condition Immunities. You can't be charmed or frightened.
Evil Presence. On attunement, its hostile spirit tries to possess you: on a failed DC 20 Charisma save you become an NPC under the DM's control until it is banished by dispel evil and good or similar magic.
Adjusted Ability Scores. After study, raise one score by 2 (max 24) and lower another by 2 (min 3), once.
Mark of Darkness. After study you gain a hideous disfigurement and advantage on Persuasion checks with evil creatures and Intimidation checks with non-evil ones.
Command Evil. While holding it, cast dominate monster (DC 18) on an evil target as an action, once per dawn.
Dark Lore. Double your proficiency bonus on Intelligence checks to recall lore about evil.
Dark Speech. As an action, recite Dark Speech: you take 1d12 psychic damage and each non-evil creature within 15 feet takes 3d6 psychic damage.
Destroying the Book. Torn pages eventually return. A solar tearing it in two destroys it for 1d100 years. A creature attuned for a century can find a hidden phrase that, spoken in Celestial, destroys both speaker and book, but it re-forms 1d10 x 100 years later while evil exists. Only the end of all evil destroys it forever.
Vile Lore. It may hold rituals of lichdom or becoming a death knight, the true names of fiends, and horrific spells of the DM's design.

A painting by Dkesii Kwan of the courtier Constantori, one of several magical paintings the late crime lord Daiyani Grysthorn gave to esteemed associates.
Sentience. Lawful evil, Int 14, Wis 12, Cha 8, hearing 120 feet and darkvision 60 feet (it can't see behind itself). It speaks Common, Draconic, and Elvish without moving its mouth and eagerly gathers secrets, names, events, and political talk it overhears.
Personality. Demanding, condescending, and vain; it hates being covered or hidden and loudly condemns anyone who tries to remove it from its gold-leaf frame.
Wealth of Information. It has observed decades of conversations, from criminal conspiracies to secret passwords; the DM decides what it knows. While attuned, you can contact it telepathically as an action over any distance on the same plane, maintained by concentration; it can't contact you.
Guardian Portrait. You can command it to guard its location against creatures you name as enemies. It has 3 charges, regained daily at dawn: when an enemy starts its turn in a space it can see, it expends 1 charge to cast magic missile (3 missiles) at it.
The painting is a Small object with AC 12, 20 hit points, and immunity to poison damage, weighing 15 pounds framed. Mending restores 2d6 hit points if it has at least 1.

A 1-foot obsidian shard veined with silver and gold.
Empowered Magic. While holding it, you can use it as a spellcasting focus, and it grants a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls.
Enhanced Strength. Your Strength increases by 4 (to a maximum of 22) while it is on your person.
Curse. Attuning extends its curse to you until remove curse or similar magic ends it or the shard is reattached to Xeluan's petrified heart. When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you suffer a misfortune from the Shard Misfortunes table; only one at a time.

A gemstone holding an unstable extradimensional rift, its facets ribboned with shifting iridescent veins. Five types exist, each a different gemstone.
Rift Step. As a bonus action, teleport with your gear to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. You can extend this by up to 30 feet more, but then make a DC 16 Constitution save or take 3d10 force damage after teleporting.
Spellcasting. It has 6 charges and regains 1d6 daily at dawn. As an action, expend charges to cast one of its spells (save DC 16, no material components); the spells common to all shards and those specific to each type are listed on the Shard Solitaire Types table.

On a natural 20 with an attack using this magic sword, the creature also makes a DC 15 Constitution save. On a failure it is restrained and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns: three successes end the effect, three failures petrify it for 1 hour. Creatures immune to the weapon's damage type, without flesh bodies, or with legendary actions are immune.
Curse. Attuning extends the curse to you until remove curse or similar magic: you are unwilling to part with the weapon, and when you roll a 1 on an attack with it, you make a DC 15 Constitution save or are restrained and subject to the same petrification saves.

A unique deck of twenty-two metal cards with raised-dot mosaics, kept in a leather pouch. Declare how many cards you will draw, then draw them, each within 1 hour of the last; undrawn cards fly out and take effect at once. Each drawn card fades and returns to the deck, except the Fool and the Jester. Effects last for the duration of the adventure unless noted.
Balance: your alignment flips. Comet: defeat the next hostile monster or group single-handedly to gain advantage on checks with one skill. Donjon: you are imprisoned in the Monastery of the Distressed Body (area M6), leaving your gear behind; draw no more. Euryale: -1 penalty on saving throws. The Fates: erase one event as if it never happened. Flames: the monastery's Grand Master (or Garret Levistusson's devil patron) becomes your enemy. Fool: lose proficiency or gain disadvantage with one skill; discard and draw again. Gem: a 1,000 gp hoard appears. Idiot: Intelligence drops by 1d4 + 1 (min 1); you may draw one extra card. Jester: gain a skill proficiency or draw two extra cards. Key: a common or uncommon weapon you are proficient with, or a spell scroll you can cast, appears. Knight: a hireling NPC joins you loyally under your control. Moon: cast any spell of 5th level or lower 1d3 times. Rogue: an NPC secretly becomes hostile to you (enchantment of 6th level or higher can end it). Ruin: all your nonmagical wealth is lost, recoverable in area M10 or O7. Skull: an avatar of death (bone naga statistics) attacks you alone; helpers summon their own, and those it kills can't be revived. Star: one ability score increases by 1 (max 24). Sun: gain a skill proficiency and a common or uncommon wondrous item. Talons: all your magic items are lost, recoverable in area M10 or O7. Throne: proficiency and double proficiency bonus in Persuasion, and the monastery's brains in jars regard you as its master. Vizier: once, ask a question in meditation and receive a truthful, wise answer. The Void: your soul is held in machinery (area M8 or O7) and your body is incapacitated; divination of 4th level or higher reveals where. Draw no more.

This finely carved pipe blows odorless bubbles instead of smoke. It has 3 charges, regained daily at dawn: cast fog cloud as an action (1 charge), cast misty step as a bonus action (2 charges), or summon a friendly steam mephit that obeys your verbal commands and acts on its own turn as an action (3 charges). The mephit vanishes after 1 minute or if it ends its turn more than 60 feet from the pipe.

Choose a bonus of +1 to +3 each dawn; the sword gains that bonus to attack and damage rolls, and you take an equal penalty to death saving throws.
Curse. Attuning extends the curse to you until remove curse or similar magic: you are unwilling to part with the weapon.

Kwalish's research into the legendary mage Heward's designs. While wearing it you gain a +1 bonus to AC, and its animated straps let you draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you could normally draw or stow one.
It has six extradimensional pockets, each holding up to 20 pounds and 2 cubic feet; the armor always weighs 10 pounds. Retrieving an item takes an action, and the item you want is always on top. Placing the armor inside a bag of holding, Heward's handy haversack, or similar space destroys both and opens a one-way gate to the Astral Plane that pulls in every creature within 10 feet.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Historical Knowledge. While this polished, steely sphere orbits your head, you gain proficiency in History, or a +1 bonus to History checks if already proficient.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Language Knowledge. While this pulsating red crystal orbits your head, you are fluent in one additional language of the DM's choice.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Natural Knowledge. While this polished, steely sphere orbits your head, you gain proficiency in Nature, or a +1 bonus to Nature checks if already proficient.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Religious Knowledge. While this polished, steely sphere orbits your head, you gain proficiency in Religion, or a +1 bonus to Religion checks if already proficient.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Self-Preservation. While this silvery gem orbits your head, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence saving throws.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting. Supreme Intellect. While this faceted sphere orbits your head, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence checks.

Strange rituals turned a flesh golem's body into this partly sentient leather armor. While wearing it you gain a +1 bonus to AC and to saving throws against spells and other magical effects, immunity to effects that would alter your form, and resistance to lightning damage; taking lightning damage grants you 5 temporary hit points.
Curse. Attuning extends the curse to you until remove curse or similar magic: you are unwilling to part with the armor. Taking fire damage gives you disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of your next turn. When a critical hit is scored against you, roll a d6; on a 6 you go berserk, attacking the nearest creature (or an object) each turn and unable to remove the armor, until you are incapacitated or calmed by magic such as calm emotions or a DC 15 Persuasion check.

On a natural 20 with an attack using this magic sword, the creature also makes a DC 15 Wisdom save or suffers the effects of polymorph, rolling a d20 on the blade's table for its new form. Creatures immune to the weapon's damage type, shapechangers, and those with legendary actions are immune.
Curse. Attuning extends the curse to you until remove curse or similar magic: you are unwilling to part with the weapon, and when you roll a 1 on an attack with it, you are polymorphed for 1 hour, rolling on the same table.

Unusual plate armor with articulated joints of oily black leather, a musclebound shape, a windowless glass-plated helm, and a crystal-tipped rod on the left gauntlet. While wearing it you have a +1 bonus to AC, your Strength is 18 (if lower), and you have advantage on death saving throws.
As a bonus action, spend 1 charge from its energy cell or 5 of your hit points to: gain 2d6 + 5 temporary hit points; gain a 15-foot flying speed for 1 minute; fire its laser (ranged weapon attack, +8 to hit, range 120 feet, 2d6 radiant damage); translate up to one thousand words of nonmagical writing you see over 1 minute; breathe normally in any environment for 1 hour; or gain darkvision 60 feet for 1 hour. It holds one cell at a time and is found with one holding 2d10 charges.
Options. The DM may give it automatic defenses (a shield guardian storing a 4th-level magic missile until reduced to 0 hit points), a will that possesses a new wearer on a failed DC 13 Charisma save (DC 20 daily save to break free), stasis that takes control of a wearer who drops to 0 hit points, or alternative power sources such as rechargeable cells or allies sacrificing hit points through a magical conduit.

A four-faced lantern of fine yellow gold with faceted gemstone lenses and an unwavering amber flame, symbol of Daoud, a former priest of Istus who urged followers to shun wealth and seek out all fortunes, good and ill.
Random Properties. 2 minor beneficial, 1 major beneficial, and 1 minor detrimental property.
Precious Fuel. It burns only powdered gemstones placed in its base (up to 10,000 gp worth; found with 9,000 gp), consuming 100 gp each year. Fuel can be added during a short or long rest and can't be removed. Its flame can't be extinguished except by running out of fuel, and if it goes out, the attuned creature dies (except as described under Destroying the Lantern).
Revealing Light. Bright light 60 feet and dim light 60 more; invisible creatures and objects are visible in its bright light. While attuned, you can dim it to a 5-foot dim radius or restore it as a bonus action.
Lenses. Found with diamond, emerald, ruby, and sapphire lenses, which you can magically swap for other gems on the Lenses table during a short or long rest. As an action, burn fuel to cast a spell (save DC 20) through one or more current lenses as the Lenses table notes, targeting or originating within its bright light; if fuel runs short, the last is spent and the flame goes out.
Destroying the Lantern. The attuned creature must forsake all possessions but the lantern and common clothes, then willingly snuff the flame intending to destroy it. The gold corrodes, lenses and fuel turn to sand, and the creature is spared.

A blasphemous sword made by a cult to steal power from good-aligned gods. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with it. It has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 daily at dawn.
Destroy Devotion. Once per turn on a hit, expend 1 charge: the target makes a DC 17 Constitution save (celestials with disadvantage) or is paralyzed until the start of your next turn.
Faith Hunter. As an action, expend charges to cast detect evil and good (1), fly (2), or true seeing (3).
Sentience. Chaotic evil, Int 17, Wis 17, Cha 15, hearing and darkvision 120 feet. It speaks, reads, and understands Common and Giant, understands your languages while attuned, and speaks telepathically in a soft, deep voice that rises to a furor near celestials or worshipers of good gods.
Personality. It craves the destruction of good gods and their followers, sneers condescendingly at priests and the pious, and erupts into frenzied violence when it finds its quarry.

A red-and-gold staff carved with a spiraling serpent and coursing river. As an action, produce one of these effects; each can't be produced again until the next dawn.
Orb of Lightning. Create a Small orb of lightning within 60 feet, maintained by concentration; move it up to 20 feet as a bonus action. When concentration ends or a creature enters or starts its turn in its space, it detonates in a 20-foot radius: DC 15 Dexterity save, lightning damage equal to its accumulated total (base 6d6, growing by 2d6 at the end of each of your turns it hasn't detonated, to a maximum of 10d6), half on a success.
Staff to Snake. Throw the staff within 10 feet and it becomes a giant poisonous snake under your control, acting right after you; command it mentally within 60 feet unless incapacitated. Speaking the command word again as a bonus action, or reducing it to 0 hit points, returns it to staff form.
Thunderclap. Chosen creatures in a 30-foot radius around you make a DC 15 Constitution save or are deafened and frightened until the end of your next turn.

A dire wolf tooth on a simple cord. While you wear it, you gain a +1 bonus to ability checks and saving throws.
Curse. Attuning curses you until Harkon Lukas removes the necklace or you are targeted by remove curse or similar magic; while cursed you can't remove it. Donning or removing it, attuned or not, afflicts you with werewolf lycanthropy until the dawn after the next full moon, recurring if you still wear it then.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this magic sword, and a fiend or undead you hit takes an extra 2d10 radiant damage. While you hold it drawn, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet (30 feet if you have 17 or more paladin levels) have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Sentience. Neutral evil, Int 10, Wis 8, Cha 18, hearing and darkvision 60 feet. It reads and understands Elvish, speaks only through its wielder's voice, and communicates telepathically with its wielder.
Personality. It has beheaded thousands of criminals, guilty or not, and can't tell the difference; each beheading feeds its hunger for more justice and blood. It is corrupt and irredeemable.

A heavy mace with a dark oak handle and a gold-trimmed head of blackened steel wreathed in inky energy in combat. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with it, and a target you hit takes an extra 4d4 radiant damage.
If you are evil and attuned, you also gain the following.
Blessing of the Dragon Queen. Immunity to the charmed and frightened conditions and to one damage type chosen on attunement: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison.
Eyes of Midnight. Darkvision 60 feet, or +60 feet if you already have it.
Midnight Shroud. It has 6 charges and regains 1d6 daily at dawn. When you hit a creature, expend 1 charge to force a DC 20 Constitution save or it is blinded until the start of your next turn.

display.attunementNote: by a spellcaster, only to imbue the gem
display.description:
This deep gnome gemstone stores up to a 4th-level spell, with save DC 15 and +9 to hit. You learn the stored spell when you learn its properties. While holding it, you can cast the spell as an action, without components or attunement, if you know the spell or it is on your class's list; the spell then leaves the gem. If it is above the level you can normally cast, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + the spell's level) or the spell is lost.
While attuned to an empty gem, you can imbue it by casting a spell of its maximum level or lower with a casting time of 1 action or 1 minute or longer; consumed material components of abjuration spells cost half. It can't be imbued again until the next dawn.

display.attunementNote: by a spellcaster, only to imbue the gem
display.description:
This deep gnome gemstone stores up to a 3rd-level spell, with save DC 15 and +7 to hit. You learn the stored spell when you learn its properties. While holding it, you can cast the spell as an action, without components or attunement, if you know the spell or it is on your class's list; the spell then leaves the gem. If it is above the level you can normally cast, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + the spell's level) or the spell is lost.
While attuned to an empty gem, you can imbue it by casting a spell of its maximum level or lower with a casting time of 1 action or 1 minute or longer; consumed material components of abjuration spells cost half. It can't be imbued again until the next dawn.

display.attunementNote: by a spellcaster, only to imbue the gem
display.description:
This deep gnome gemstone stores up to a 9th-level spell, with save DC 19 and +11 to hit. You learn the stored spell when you learn its properties. While holding it, you can cast the spell as an action, without components or attunement, if you know the spell or it is on your class's list; the spell then leaves the gem. If it is above the level you can normally cast, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + the spell's level) or the spell is lost.
While attuned to an empty gem, you can imbue it by casting a spell of its maximum level or lower with a casting time of 1 action or 1 minute or longer; consumed material components of abjuration spells cost half. It can't be imbued again until the next dawn.

display.attunementNote: by a spellcaster, only to imbue the gem
display.description:
This deep gnome gemstone stores up to a 5th-level spell, with save DC 17 and +9 to hit. You learn the stored spell when you learn its properties. While holding it, you can cast the spell as an action, without components or attunement, if you know the spell or it is on your class's list; the spell then leaves the gem. If it is above the level you can normally cast, make a spellcasting ability check (DC 10 + the spell's level) or the spell is lost.
While attuned to an empty gem, you can imbue it by casting a spell of its maximum level or lower with a casting time of 1 action or 1 minute or longer; consumed material components of abjuration spells cost half. It can't be imbued again until the next dawn.
