A clear potion flecked with dark red, like clotted blood. Drinking it removes a curse of lycanthropy imposed by a lycanthrope's bite or similar effect.

Holding one end, you can speak its command word as an action to lash the other end at a beast you can see within 20 feet. It makes a DC 17 Charisma save or the bridle ties around its neck and it falls under your command as if by dominate beast; you no longer need to hold the bridle. On a success it is immune until the next dawn. You can release a bound creature as a bonus action, and it makes a DC 17 Charisma check each dawn to break free.

While wearing this crown, you automatically fail Investigation checks to see through illusions; touching an illusion still reveals it, but you feel so strongly it is real that you may not know which sense to trust. A DC 20 Nature or Perception check on close examination, or detect magic cast at 3rd level or higher, reveals its nature.

When you toss this Ioun stone into the air as an action, it orbits your head at 1d3 feet. Another creature must use an action and hit AC 24 or succeed on a DC 24 Acrobatics check to grasp or net it; you can seize and stow it as an action. It has AC 24, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage, and counts as a worn object while orbiting.
Vitality. While this luminous green-and-blue marbled sphere orbits your head, you gain a +1 bonus to death saving throws.
White dust swirls within this pale gray potion. Drinking it cures you of mummy rot.

Moghadam's sword, its hilt a jade devil face from which a blade that always looks rusted and ruined extends, reflecting its surroundings as if decayed. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with it, and undead you hit take an extra 1d8 force damage.
Blighted Ruin. Cast blight (DC 15) from it once per dawn.
Destructive Ruin. Cast disintegrate against a nonmagical object or creation of magical force, once every seven days.
Curse. Attuning extends the curse to you until remove curse or similar magic: you are unwilling to part with it, and it must help destroy 1,000 gp of materials every seven days or a conflict arises between you.
Sentience. Lawful evil, Int 15, Wis 8, Cha 16, hearing and darkvision 120 feet. It speaks, reads, and understands Common, understands your languages while attuned, and speaks telepathically in a rough, ruined echo.
Personality. Dolorous or frenetic by mood, happiest when destroying. It urges constant ruin so its owner can rebuild the world from a blank slate.

name: The Infernal Machine of Lum the Mad
spoken: the infernal machine of lum the mad

display.description:
The command console of a planar craft that crashed in the Barrier Peaks, later used by Baron Lum to build his empire. It weighs some 5,500 pounds and is worked by sixty levers, forty dials, twenty switches, and jeweled components. Its effects use save DC 14 or your spell save DC, whichever is higher.
Silver Wire. It can produce an invisible, astral silver wire of virtually infinite length that tethers it to its attuned user, letting them use its powers centered on themselves and concentrate on its effects remotely. If the wire is cut (only by effects that can cut an astral projection's silver cord), the user dies instantly.
Summon Monster. 1/day each: conjure animals, summon lesser demons. 1/7 days each: conjure minor elementals, conjure woodland beings, summon greater demon. 1/month each: conjure elemental, conjure fey.
Wish. Once per month it can produce wish, side effects included; each use adds a cumulative 10 percent chance of malfunction, requiring seven days and 500 gp of repairs (which reset the chance to 10 percent).
Random Properties. At the end of each of the attuned user's long rests, it generates 1d4 + 1 beneficial and 1d4 + 1 detrimental properties from the Infernal Machine Properties table, lasting until the next long rest.
Destroying the Machine. It repairs anything short of catastrophic damage. Rumor holds that one control combination puts it in a repair mode that allows access and stops self-repair, and another teleports its critical parts away into space and time.
This potion seems to change color and texture each time you look at it. Drinking it ends a polymorph effect imposed by thessaltoxin.
A greatsword of unknown black metal. It is a +1 greatsword, but works as a +3 greatsword against a thessalhydra, and as a +4 greatsword while in the Upside Down.
A +2 mace. Whenever it is used to destroy an undead creature, a single silver piece appears in the wielder's pocket.

A small object of rune-covered, multicolored metal parts linked by gears and bands that shines with a rainbow in the light. Arm it by turning its key as a bonus action, then hurl it up to 120 feet as an action; it explodes at the end of your turn. Creatures within 60 feet make a DC 15 Dexterity save (28 (8d6) fire damage, half on success) and a DC 15 Constitution save (28 (8d6) thunder damage and stunned until the end of their next turn, or half and not stunned). The wielder also rolls three times on the wand of wonder table, rerolling duplicates: targeted effects hit all creatures in range, and effects on the wielder hit the creature nearest the grenade. It explodes at once if placed in an extradimensional space or if its holder teleports, affecting creatures within 30 feet of both ends.

A fiery red crystal the size of a human palm. Once per day as a bonus action, a villain can activate it to undo one deed, such as rewinding an action to take it again or rerolling a failed saving throw. Each use erases someone the wielder knows: roll a d20, and on 5-20 one of their allies disintegrates, on 1-4 one of the player characters does. If a creature bound its soul to it in the "Thalivar's Beacon" quest, it explodes when used, and the bound creature disintegrates, returnable only by wish or similar magic.

A glass orb holding a hovering, ignited delerium shard crackling with colored energy.
As an action you throw it up to 30 feet; it bursts in a 20-foot radius. Each creature there makes a DC 15 Constitution save or takes 8d6 necrotic and gains a level of contamination, and an arcane anomaly occurs at the point of impact.

While wearing this amulet you can read all writing and speak and understand any language. As an action you can cast detect thoughts, sending, or telepathic bond, each once per dawn, using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma and your proficiency bonus for its attack bonus and save DC.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.

Its head is a massive crackling delerium crystal. Hits with it deal an extra 3d6 necrotic. When you roll a 20 on an attack with it, it unleashes an arcane anomaly; roll twice and choose either result.

Attuning requires a 1-hour ceremony with six other characters, each attuned to a different Seal of Drakkenheim.
The crown has 3 charges and regains one every ten years; as an action, expend 1 to cast wish. While you wear it, Minazorond, the tower dragons, and the wall gargoyles obey your spoken commands. Seated on the Throne of Drakkenheim, as an action you can telepathically command one dragon or twelve gargoyles within 100 miles of Castle Drakken and see and hear through one of them (with its special senses) until the start of your next turn, while deaf and blind to your own surroundings.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.

A refined delerium crystal in a glass orb. While holding it you gain +2 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC, and can use it as a spellcasting focus. Once per day, when you cast a spell of 5th level or lower, you can power it from the crystal without a spell slot, triggering a random arcane anomaly.

A glowing meteoric-iron blade infused with delerium dust, a glass-encased sliver set in its hilt.
You gain +2 to attack and damage rolls with it, can use your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and can use it as a spellcasting focus. When you roll a 20 to attack a humanoid with it, the target makes a DC 15 Constitution save or takes an extra 3d6 necrotic and gains a level of contamination.

A metal lance with a burning tip, fed by a hose from a tank worn on your back.
You gain +1 to attack and damage rolls with it. The tank has 5 charges; as an action you expend 1 or more to cast burning hands (save DC 15), at 1st level for 1 charge and one level higher per extra charge. Once per day, pouring in a vial of alchemist's fire restores all charges; otherwise they don't recover.

Ammunition tipped with refined delerium. A creature hit by it takes an extra 3d6 necrotic and makes a DC 15 Constitution save or gains a level of contamination. On a hit, the tip crumbles and the ammunition becomes nonmagical.

Hermetically sealed plate armor with a visored helmet. While worn with the visor closed, you are immune to disease and the poisoned condition, have advantage on saves against effects that cause contamination, have resistance to necrotic and poison damage, and don't need to breathe.

While wearing it you see invisible creatures and objects within 60 feet, and gain +2 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC.
Relic of Saint Vitruvio. A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio can cast heal three times per long rest and can attune to two extra magic items, provided both are also Relics.

name: Ignacious, the Sword of Burning Truth
spoken: ignacious the sword of burning truth

display.description:
A sacred silver blade trailing embers first kindled in the Temple of Lumen.
You gain +3 to attack and damage rolls with it. As a bonus action you speak its name to wreathe it in radiant flame (bright light 40 feet, dim light 40 more), dealing an extra 4d6 radiant on hits until you douse it as a bonus action or drop or sheathe it.
Sentience. Lawful good, Int 11, Wis 19, Cha 23, hearing and darkvision 120 feet; it speaks, reads, and understands Common, Celestial, and Draconic, communicates telepathically, and knows its wielder's thoughts. When drawn it casts zone of truth (save DC 20) centered on itself, maintaining concentration for you.
Personality. Zealously devoted to the Sacred Flame and indifferent to the Falling Fire schism, it seeks to expose deception, always knows when it hears a lie, and a lie spoken by its wielder immediately triggers a conflict.
Relic of Saint Vitruvio. A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio can cast heal three times per long rest and can attune to two extra magic items, provided both are also Relics.

display.attunementNote: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
display.description:
A magic quarterstaff granting +2 to attack and damage rolls, and +2 to spell attack rolls and spell save DC while held.
It has 20 charges, regaining 2d10 at dawn; when you spend the last, roll a d20: on a 1 it triggers a random arcane anomaly, on a 20 it regains 1d10 charges. As an action you can spend charges to cast, with your DC and ability: haste or slow (3), arcane eye or dimension door (4), arcane hand or wall of force (5), disintegrate (6), reverse gravity (7), or maze (8). Without charges you can cast detect magic, floating disk, mage armor, mending, message, or misty step.

As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.

Once per dawn, as an action, you bellow a command audible within 300 feet; up to 12 allies you can see who hear it gain 20 temporary hit points and, while those last, advantage on attack rolls and saves.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.
Once per day, as an action while holding it, you can cast purge contamination. Afterward roll a d20; on a 1 the rod melts into sludge.

A pouch holding an ounce of purified, charged delerium dust. Consuming the full pouch as an action gives you advantage on spell attack rolls and on saves against spells for 1 minute, and you gain a level of contamination.

display.attunementNote: by a bard, cleric, druid, or paladin
display.description:
As an action you can cast bless, death ward, greater restoration, prayer of healing, or revivify from it, each once per dawn, using your spellcasting ability and save DC.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.
Relic of Saint Vitruvio. A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio can cast heal three times per long rest and can attune to two extra magic items, provided both are also Relics.

A magic quarterstaff granting +2 to attack and damage rolls. It has 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn; as an action you spend charges to cast, with your save DC: guiding bolt (1), flaming sphere (2), or flame strike (5).
Relic of Saint Vitruvio. A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio can cast heal three times per long rest and can attune to two extra magic items, provided both are also Relics.

Hammered meteoric iron set with a delerium crystal.
When a melee or ranged attack hits you, you can use your reaction to absorb its residual energy (you still take the hit), giving the shield 1 charge (maximum 5; unused charges vanish at dawn). As an action you can release all charges: each creature within 10 feet makes a DC 15 Constitution save or takes 1d6 force per charge, is flung 10 feet, and is knocked prone.

A refined meteoric-iron quarterstaff with a liquid delerium core. Once on your turn, when you hit a creature with a melee attack using it, the target makes a DC 13 Intelligence save or takes an extra 3d6 psychic, can't take reactions until the start of your next turn, and on its next turn can take only one of an action, a bonus action, or movement.
You can use it as a spellcasting focus. Creatures saving against a spell cast through it can't benefit from advantage on the save.

While wearing it you can cast disguise self at will. Once per dawn, as an action, you and your gear turn invisible for 1 minute or until you become visible as a bonus action.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.

display.attunementNote: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
display.description:
A magic quarterstaff granting +2 to attack and damage rolls.
It has 20 charges, regaining 1 for each hour it rests in the Deep Haze; touching a delerium crystal to it restores 2d8 + 4 as the crystal crumbles. Spending the last charge gives you 1d6 levels of contamination. As an action you can spend charges to cast, with your DC and ability and without gaining contamination: delerium orb (1), warp bolt (2), ride the rifts (3), delerium blast (4), conjure the deep haze (5), or ray of contamination (6).

A bow or crossbow fitted with delerium shards and lenses that conjures its own projectiles.
You gain +2 to attack and damage rolls with it; it deals radiant instead of piercing damage and ignores the ammunition and loading properties. It has 3 charges, regained at dawn; when you hit with it, you can spend 1 to make the bolt burst, and the target and each creature within 10 feet make a DC 15 Constitution save or are blinded until the end of your next turn.

While wearing this badge you can cast mage hand, prestidigitation, purify food and drink, and unseen servant at will. As an action you can cast animate objects, create food and water, dispel magic, or telekinesis, each once per dawn, using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma and your proficiency bonus for its attack bonus and save DC.
Seal of Drakkenheim. You can attune to only one Seal. Guardian constructs such as wall gargoyles and tower dragons won't attack you while you are attuned to one, unless you attack or cast a spell on that guardian (which then ignores the seal for 24 hours). As an action you can present the seal to rebuke them: make an opposed Charisma check against each such guardian within 30 feet that can see or hear you; each you beat can't move, act, or react for 1 minute or until damaged, and each that beats you is immune for 24 hours.

It has 3 charges, regained at dawn. When a spellcaster within 60 feet targets you with a spell or includes you in its area, you can spend 1 charge to cast counterspell as a reaction.
Relic of Saint Vitruvio. A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio can cast heal three times per long rest and can attune to two extra magic items, provided both are also Relics.

As an action, you can splash the contents of this vial onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw the vial up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the acid as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 acid damage.

This sticky, adhesive fluid ignites when exposed to air. As an action, you can throw this flask up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the alchemist's fire as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can end this damage by using its action to make a DC 10 Dexterity check to extinguish the flames.
A small box for alms, typically found in a priest's pack.

A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. It might be an amulet depicting a symbol representing a deity, the same symbol carefully engraved or inlaid as an emblem on a shield, or a tiny box holding a fragment of a sacred relic. Appendix B lists the symbols commonly associated with many gods in the multiverse. A cleric or paladin can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.
A creature that drinks this vial of liquid gains advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour. It confers no benefit to undead or constructs.

As an action, you can spill these tiny metal balls from their pouch to cover a level, square area that is 10 feet on a side. A creature moving across the covered area must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn't need to make the save.
A set of pulleys with a cable threaded through them and a hook to attach to objects, a block and tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.
A block of incense, typically found in a priest's pack.

A book might contain poetry, historical accounts, information pertaining to a particular field of lore, diagrams and notes on gnomish contraptions, or just about anything else that can be represented using text or pictures. A book of spells is a spellbook (described later in this section).

As an action, you can spread a bag of caltrops to cover a square area that is 5 feet on a side. Any creature that enters the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or stop moving this turn and take 1 piercing damage. Taking this damage reduces the creature's walking speed by 10 feet until the creature regains at least 1 hit point. A creature moving through the area at half speed doesn't need to make the save.
For 1 hour, a candle sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet.
This wooden case can hold up to twenty crossbow bolts.
This cylindrical leather case can hold up to ten rolled-up sheets of paper or five rolled-up sheets of parchment.
A censer, typically found in a priest's pack.
A chain has 10 hit points. It can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength check.

A climber's kit includes special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness. You can use the climber's kit as an action to anchor yourself; when you do, you can't fall more than 25 feet from the point where you anchored yourself, and you can't climb more than 25 feet away from that point without undoing the anchor.

A component pouch is a small, watertight leather belt pouch that has compartments to hold all the material components and other special items you need to cast your spells, except for those components that have a specific cost (as indicated in a spell's description).
Using a crowbar grants advantage to Strength checks where the crowbar's leverage can be applied.

An arcane focus is a special item--an orb, a crystal, a rod, a specially constructed staff, a wand-like length of wood, or some similar item--designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus.

This pouch of cosmetics, hair dye, and small props lets you create disguises that change your physical appearance. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a visual disguise.

A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. It might be an amulet depicting a symbol representing a deity, the same symbol carefully engraved or inlaid as an emblem on a shield, or a tiny box holding a fragment of a sacred relic. Appendix B lists the symbols commonly associated with many gods in the multiverse. A cleric or paladin can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.
This kit includes a wooden rod, silken line, corkwood bobbers, steel hooks, lead sinkers, velvet lures, and narrow netting.

This small box contains a variety of papers and parchments, pens and inks, seals and sealing wax, gold and silver leaf, and other supplies necessary to create convincing forgeries of physical documents. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to create a physical forgery of a document.

This kit is a leather pouch containing bandages, salves, and splints. The kit has ten uses. As an action, you can expend one use of the kit to stabilize a creature that has 0 hit points, without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

This kit contains a variety of instruments such as clippers, mortar and pestle, and pouches and vials used by herbalists to create remedies and potions. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to identify or apply herbs. Also, proficiency with this kit is required to create antitoxin and potions of healing.

As an action, you can splash the contents of this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. In either case, make a ranged attack against a target creature, treating the holy water as an improvised weapon. If the target is a fiend or undead, it takes 2d6 radiant damage. A cleric or paladin may create holy water by performing a special ritual. The ritual takes 1 hour to perform, uses 25 gp worth of powdered silver, and requires the caster to expend a 1st-level spell slot.

When you use your action to set it, this trap forms a saw-toothed steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and stop moving. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet long). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 piercing damage to the trapped creature.
A lamp casts bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.
A bullseye lantern casts bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil.

A hooded lantern casts bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil. As an action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.
A small bag of sand, typically found in a scholar's pack.

A key is provided with the lock. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick this lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Your GM may decide that better locks are available for higher prices.

This lens allows a closer look at small objects. It is also useful as a substitute for flint and steel when starting fires. Lighting a fire with a magnifying glass requires light as bright as sunlight to focus, tinder to ignite, and about 5 minutes for the fire to ignite. A magnifying glass grants advantage on any ability check made to appraise or inspect an item that is small or highly detailed.

These metal restraints can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the manacles requires a successful DC 20 Dexterity check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of manacles comes with one key. Without the key, a creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick the manacles' lock with a successful DC 15 Dexterity check. Manacles have 15 hit points.
This tin box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl.

Oil usually comes in a clay flask that holds 1 pint. As an action, you can splash the oil in this flask onto a creature within 5 feet of you or throw it up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a target creature or object, treating the oil as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target is covered in oil. If the target takes any fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an additional 5 fire damage from the burning oil. You can also pour a flask of oil on the ground to cover a 5-foot-square area, provided that the surface is level. If lit, the oil burns for 2 rounds and deals 5 fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn in the area. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

An arcane focus is a special item--an orb, a crystal, a rod, a specially constructed staff, a wand-like length of wood, or some similar item--designed to channel the power of arcane spells. A sorcerer, warlock, or wizard can use such an item as a spellcasting focus.

You can use the poison in this vial to coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition. Applying the poison takes an action. A creature hit by the poisoned weapon or ammunition must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 1d4 poison damage. Once applied, the poison retains potency for 1 minute before drying.

A poisoner's kit includes the vials, chemicals, and other equipment necessary for the creation of poisons. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to craft or use poisons.

A cloth or leather pouch can hold up to 20 sling bullets or 50 blowgun needles, among other things. A compartmentalized pouch for holding spell components is called a component pouch (described earlier in this section).
A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.
You can use a portable ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check.
Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. It might be an amulet depicting a symbol representing a deity, the same symbol carefully engraved or inlaid as an emblem on a shield, or a tiny box holding a fragment of a sacred relic. Appendix B lists the symbols commonly associated with many gods in the multiverse. A cleric or paladin can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.

A scale includes a small balance, pans, and a suitable assortment of weights up to 2 pounds. With it, you can measure the exact weight of small objects, such as raw precious metals or trade goods, to help determine their worth.
A small knife, typically found in a scholar's pack.
Essential for wizards, a spellbook is a leather-bound tome with 100 blank vellum pages suitable for recording spells.

A druidic focus might be a sprig of mistletoe or holly, a wand or scepter made of yew or another special wood, a staff drawn whole out of a living tree, or a totem object incorporating feathers, fur, bones, and teeth from sacred animals. A druid can use such an object as a spellcasting focus.
Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch--or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel--takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.
A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

A blinded creature can't see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
A charmed creature can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects. The charmer has advantage on any ability check to interact socially with the creature.
A deafened creature can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.
A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight. The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

A grappled creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated, or if the creature is removed from the grappler's reach by an effect such as Thunderwave.
An incapacitated creature can't take actions or reactions.

An invisible creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense; for hiding, it is heavily obscured. Its location can be detected by noise or tracks. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage, and its attack rolls have advantage.

A paralyzed creature is incapacitated and can't move or speak. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and any attack that hits it is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet.

A petrified creature is transformed, along with any nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it ceases aging. It is incapacitated, can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves. It has resistance to all damage and is immune to poison and disease.
A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition. It has disadvantage on attack rolls. An attack roll against it has advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet, otherwise disadvantage.

A restrained creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and its attack rolls have disadvantage. It has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.
A stunned creature is incapacitated, can't move, and can speak only falteringly. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Attack rolls against it have advantage.

An unconscious creature is incapacitated, can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings. It drops whatever it's holding and falls prone. It automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and any attack that hits it is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet.

Exhaustion is measured in six levels, and effects are cumulative. Level 1: disadvantage on ability checks. Level 2: speed halved. Level 3: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws. Level 4: hit point maximum halved. Level 5: speed reduced to 0. Level 6: death. A creature removes one level of exhaustion when it finishes a long rest, provided it has also ingested some food and drink.

+1 Constitution, gain a cantrip and 1st level spell Buff, Debuff Prerequisite: No other dragonmark You have manifested an aberrant dragonmark. Determine its appearance and the flaw associated with it. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn a cantrip of your choice from the sorcerer spell list. In addition, choose a 1st-level spell from the sorcerer spell list. You learn that spell and can cast it through your mark. Once you cast it, you must finish a short or long rest before you can cast it again through the mark. Constitution is your spellcasting ability for these spells. When you cast the 1st-level spell through your mark, you can expend one of your Hit Dice and roll it. If you roll an even number, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the number rolled. If you roll an odd number, one random creature within 30 feet of you (not including you) takes force damage equal to the number rolled. If no other creatures are in range, you take the damage. You also develop a random flaw from the Aberrant Dragonmark Flaws table. Aberrant Dragonmark Flaws OPTION: GREATER ABERRANT POWERS At the DM’s option, a character who has the Aberrant Dragonmark feat has a chance of manifesting greater power. Upon reaching 10th level, such a character has a 10 percent chance of gaining an epic boon from among the options in chapter 7 of the Dungeon Master’s Guide. If the character fails to gain a boon, they have a 10 percent chance the next time they gain a level. If the character gains a boon, the DM chooses it or determines it randomly. The character also permanently loses one of their Hit Dice, and their hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to a roll of that die plus their Constitution modifier (minimum reduction of 1). This reduction can’t be reversed by any means.

display.prerequisite: 4th Level, Initiate of High Sorcery (Lunitari) Feat
display.description: +1 Charisma, skilled at mimicry and dramatics Buff, Social, Deception Adept of the Black Robes

+5 Initiative, can't be surprised, no advantage for hidden attackers Buff, Detection Always on the lookout for danger, you gain the following benefits: You gain a +5 bonus to initiative. You can't be surprised while you are conscious. Other creatures don’t gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.

+1 Strength or Dexterity - you have undergone extensive physical training Buff, Movement, Exploration You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of your movement. Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement. You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

Make a melee attack or shove after the Dash action Movement, Combat When you use your action to Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to shove a creature. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack’s damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

+1 Constitution or Wisdom, Cook's Utensils proficiency, cook special food Healing, Buff Time spent mastering the culinary arts has paid off , granting you the following benefits: Increase your Constitution or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with cook’s utensils if you don’t already have it. As part of a short rest, you can cook special food, provided you have ingredients and cook’s utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. At the end of the short rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points regains an extra 1d8 hit points. With one hour of work or when you finish a long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

No loading, no within 5 ft. disadvantage, bonus action attack with hand crossbow Thanks to extensive practice with the crossbow, you gain the following benefits: You ignore the loading property of crossbows with which you are proficient. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn’t impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls. When you use the Attack action and attack with a one-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with a hand crossbow you are holding.

Add your proficiency bonus to your AC as a reaction Combat, Warding Prerequisite: Dexterity 13 or higher When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

+1 AC bonus, wield heavier weapons, draw or stow two weapons at once Buff, Combat You master fighting with two weapons, gaining the following benefits: You gain a +1 bonus to AC while you are wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand. You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one-handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light. You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.

You are alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many dungeons Buff, Detection, Warding Alert to the hidden traps and secret doors found in many dungeons, you gain the following benefits: You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to detect the presence of secret doors. You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid or resist traps. You have resistance to the damage dealt by traps. Traveling at a fast pace doesn't impose the normal −5 penalty on your passive Wisdom (Perception) score.

+1 Constitution, minimum Con modifier x2 on spent Hit Dice Healing, Buff Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits: Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum number of hit points you regain from the roll equals twice your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).

display.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
display.description: Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type Damage, Control Prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2. You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, learn misty step and another 1st level spell Buff, Utility Your exposure to the Feywild’s magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the misty step spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the divination or enchantment school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can’t cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells’ spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

You’ve developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits: You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are grappling. You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you. To do so, make another grapple check. If you succeed, you and the creature are both restrained until the grapple ends.

You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage Damage, Combat You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action. Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

You are an able physician, allowing you to mend wounds quickly and get your allies back in the fight. You gain the following benefits: When you use a healer's kit to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point. As an action, you can spend one use of a healer's kit to tend to a creature and restore 1d6 + 4 hit points to it, plus additional hit points equal to the creature's maximum number of Hit Dice. The creature can't regain hit points from this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.
You have trained to master the use of heavy armor, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

+1 Strength, damage reduction from nonmagical weapons Buff, Warding Prerequisite: Proficiency with heavy armor You can use your armor to deflect strikes that would kill others. You gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20. While you are wearing heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 3.

Inspire your companions to grant temporary hit points Healing, Buff, Social Prerequisite: Charisma 13 or higher You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.

+1 Intelligence, track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision Buff, Utility, Exploration You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits. Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You always know which way is north. You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset. You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

+1 Strength or Dexterity, proficiency with light armor Buff, Warding You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with light armor.

+1 Intelligence, additional languages, create written ciphers Buff, Utility You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn three languages of your choice. You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

You have inexplicable luck that seems to kick in at just the right moment. You have 3 luck points. Whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can spend one luck point to roll an additional d20. You can choose to spend one of your luck points after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You choose which of the d20s is used for the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. You can also spend one luck point when an attack roll is made against you. Roll a d20, and then choose whether the attack uses the attacker's roll or yours. If more than one creature spends a luck point to influence the outcome of a roll, the points cancel each other out; no additional dice are rolled. You regain your expended luck points when you finish a long rest.

You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters Buff, Debuff, Combat You have practiced techniques useful in melee combat against spellcasters, gaining the following benefits: When a creature within 5 feet of you casts a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature. When you damage a creature that is concentrating on a spell, that creature has disadvantage on the saving throw it makes to maintain its concentration. You have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by creatures within 5 feet of you.

Learn basic spells from a chosen class Buff, Utility Choose a class: bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard. You learn two cantrips of your choice from that class’s spell list. In addition, choose one 1st-level spell to learn from that same list. Using this feat, you can cast the spell once at its lowest level, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it in this way again. Your spellcasting ability for these spells depends on the class you chose: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat maneuvers. You gain the following benefits: You learn two maneuvers of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype in the fighter class. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice). You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

You have practiced moving in medium armor Buff, Warding Prerequisite: Proficiency with medium armor You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits: Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity (Stealth) checks. When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

You are exceptionally speedy and agile. You gain the following benefits: Your speed increases by 10 feet. When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn. When you make a melee attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or not.

+1 Strength or Dexterity, proficiency with medium armor and shields Buff, Warding Prerequisite: Proficiency with light armor You have trained to master the use of medium armor and shields, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with medium armor and shields.

You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted Buff, Warding You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't incapacitated, you gain the following benefits: You have advantage on melee attack rolls against any unmounted creature that is smaller than your mount. You can force an attack targeted at your mount to target you instead. If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.

+1 Intelligence or Wisdom, quick to notice details of your environment Buff, Detection Quick to notice details of your environment, you gain the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20. If you can see a creature's mouth while it is speaking a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips. You have a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.

+1 Strength, or Dexterity, reroll damage dice for piercing damage You have achieved a penetrating precision in combat, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals piercing damage, you can reroll one of the attack’s damage dice, and you must use the new roll. When you score a critical hit that deals piercing damage to a creature, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the extra piercing damage the target takes.

Learn to make and use poisons in combat Buff, Combat You can prepare and deliver deadly poisons, granting you the following benefits: When you make a damage roll that deals poison damage, it ignores resistance to poison damage. You can apply poison to a weapon or piece of ammunition as a bonus action, instead of an action. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner's Kit if you don’t already have it. With one hour of work using a poisoner’s kit and expending 50 gp worth of materials, you can create a number of doses of potent poison equal to your proficiency bonus. Once applied to a weapon or piece of ammunition, the poison retains its potency for 1 minute or until you hit with the weapon or ammunition. When a creature takes damage from the coated weapon or ammunition, that creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 poison damage and become poisoned until the end of your next turn.

You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons Control, Combat You gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon’s damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, quarterstaff, or spear, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.

+1 stat and proficiency with saving throws to a chosen ability score Buff, Warding Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.

display.prerequisite: Intelligence or Wisdom of 13 or higher
display.description: You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals Prerequisite: Intelligence or Wisdom of 13 or higher You have learned a number of spells that you can cast as rituals. These spells are written in a ritual book, which you must have in hand while casting one of them. When you choose this feat, you acquire a ritual book holding two 1st-level spells of your choice. Choose one of the following classes: bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard. You must choose your spells from that class’s spell list, and the spells you choose must have the ritual tag. The class you choose also determines your spellcasting ability for these spells: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard. If you come across a spell in written form, such as a magical spell scroll or a wizard’s spellbook, you might be able to add it to your ritual book. The spell must be on the spell list for the class you chose, the spell’s level can be no higher than half your level (rounded up), and it must have the ritual tag. The process of copying the spell into your ritual book takes 2 hours per level of the spell, and costs 50 gp per level. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it.
Reroll damage dice for melee weapon attacks Damage, Combat Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon’s damage dice and use either total.

Take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard Control, Warding You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn. Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach. When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, learn invisibility and another 1st level spell Buff, Utility Your exposure to the Shadowfell’s magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the invisibility spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice. The 1st-level spell must be from the illusion or necromancy school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either of these spells in this way, you can’t cast that spell in this way again until you finish a long rest. You can also cast these spells using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. The spells’ spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat.

Ranged weapons mastery - make shots that others find impossible Damage, Buff You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits: Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls. Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover. Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

Use shields not just for protection but also for offense Damage, Combat, Warding You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a shield: If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to shove a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield. If you aren't incapacitated, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you. If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.

+1 to an ability score, +1 proficiency, expertise You have honed your proficiency with particular skills, granting you the following benefits: Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice. Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn’t already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.
You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

You are expert at slinking through shadows Buff, Deception Prerequisite: Dexterity 13 or higher You are expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits: You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding. When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position. Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight.

+1 Strength, or Dexterity, wound and disable targets with bladed weapons Buff, Combat You’ve learned where to cut to have the greatest results, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20. Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack that deals slashing damage, you can reduce the speed of the target by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. When you score a critical hit that deals slashing damage to a creature, you grievously wound it. Until the start of your next turn, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls.

display.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
display.description: Enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells Buff, Combat Prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell You have learned techniques to enhance your attacks with certain kinds of spells, gaining the following benefits: When you cast a spell that requires you to make an attack roll, the spell’s range is doubled. Your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover. You learn one cantrip that requires an attack roll. Choose the cantrip from the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. Your spellcasting ability for this cantrip depends on the spell list you chose from: Charisma for bard, sorcerer, or warlock; Wisdom for cleric or druid; or Intelligence for wizard.

Inherit the innate spellcasting ability of your ancestors Deception, Warding, Species Feat Prerequisite: Gnome (deep gnome) You have inherited the innate spellcasting ability of your ancestors. This ability allows you to cast nondetection on yourself at will, without needing a material component. You can also cast each of the following spells once with this ability: blindness/deafness, blur, and disguise self. You regain the ability to cast these spells when you finish a long rest. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you cast them at their lowest possible levels.

+1 Strength or Constitution, improved improvised weapons Damage, Utility, Combat Accustomed to rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You are proficient with improvised weapons. Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, learn mage hand, and move things with your mind. Control You learn to move things with your mind, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the mage hand cantrip. You can cast it without verbal or somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand invisible. If you already know this spell, its range increases by 30 feet when you cast it. Its spellcasting ability is the ability increased by this feat. As a bonus action, you can try to telekinetically shove one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. When you do so, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat) or be moved 5 feet toward you or away from you. A creature can willingly fail this save.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. Telepathy 60 ft. Communication, Psionic You awaken the ability to mentally connect with others, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Your telepathic utterances are in a language you know, and the creature understands you only if it knows that language. Your communication doesn’t give the creature the ability to respond to you telepathically. You can cast the detect thoughts spell, requiring no spell slot or components, and you must finish a long rest before you can cast it this way again. Your spellcasting ability for the spell is the ability increased by this feat. If you have spell slots of 2nd level or higher, you can cast this spell with them.

Gain +2 hit points per character level Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

display.prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell
display.description: You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat Combat, Warding Prerequisite: The ability to cast at least one spell You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat, learning techniques that grant you the following benefits: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws that you make to maintain your concentration on a spell when you take damage. You can perform the somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a shield in one or both hands. When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to cast a spell at the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action and must target only that creature.

+1 Strength or Dexterity, 4 additional weapon proficiencies Buff, Combat You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits: Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice. Each one must be a simple or a martial weapon.
Reaction when an ally you can see within 30 feet rolls a 1 on an attack, check or save: it rerolls and must use the new roll. You can't use Lucky until the end of your next turn.

+1 Str, Con or Cha. Spend a Breath Weapon use to roar instead: chosen creatures within 30 feet that can see or hear you make a Wis save (DC 8 + proficiency + Cha) or are frightened for 1 minute, repeating the save when they take damage.
+1 Str, Con or Cha. Unarmored AC 13 + Dex (shields allowed). Retractable claws: unarmed strikes deal 1d4 + Str slashing.
Detect magic at will; levitate and dispel magic once each per long rest without a slot. Charisma is the spellcasting ability.
+1 Con. When you take the Dodge action in combat, spend a Hit Die to heal its roll + Con mod (min 1).
+1 Dex, Int, Wis or Cha. With advantage on an attack using Dex, Int, Wis or Cha, reroll one of the dice once.
+1 Dex or Int. Reaction right after taking damage: invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack, deal damage or force a save. Once per short or long rest.
+1 Int or Cha. Speak, read and write Sylvan. Misty step once per short or long rest without a slot (Intelligence).

+1 Int or Cha. Reroll 1s on your spells' fire damage dice (must keep the reroll). After casting a fire spell, flames wreathe you until the end of your next turn: bright light 30 feet, dim 30 more, and a creature within 5 feet that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d4 fire.
+1 Con. Resistance to cold and poison damage; advantage on saves against being poisoned.
+1 Str or Con. Once per short or long rest, on a simple or martial weapon hit, roll one weapon damage die again and add it. Right after Relentless Endurance, reaction to make one weapon attack.
One skill, one tool and one language of your choice, plus expertise in one skill you're proficient in that isn't already doubled.
+1 Dex, Con or Cha. Reaction when a creature you can see hits you with an attack: it rerolls. Usable again after you roll initiative or finish a short or long rest.
+1 Str or Dex. +5 feet walking speed. Proficiency in Acrobatics or Athletics. Advantage on Athletics or Acrobatics checks to escape a grapple.
One druid cantrip of your choice; longstrider and pass without trace once each per long rest without a slot. Wisdom is the spellcasting ability.

One artificer cantrip and one 1st-level artificer spell (Intelligence); cast the 1st-level spell once per long rest without a slot or with your slots. Proficiency with one artisan's tool, usable as a focus for your Intelligence spells.
Learn one Eldritch Invocation (Int, Wis or Cha, chosen now); one with a prerequisite only if you're a warlock who meets it. Swap it when you gain a level.
Learn one fighter Fighting Style you don't have; swap it at levels that grant an Ability Score Improvement.
+1 Dex. Proficiency with firearms, ignore their loading property, and no disadvantage on ranged attacks for being within 5 feet of a hostile creature.

Learn two sorcerer Metamagic options (one per spell unless an option says otherwise; swap one at Ability Score Improvement levels) and 2 sorcery points usable only on Metamagic, regained on a long rest.
+1 Strength or Dexterity (max 20). While wielding a double-bladed scimitar with two hands, +1 AC, and it has the finesse property for you.

Forged by Purphoros. Constructed Resilience: advantage on saves against being poisoned and resistance to poison; no need to eat, drink, breathe or sleep; immune to disease; magic can't put you to sleep. Sentry's Rest: a long rest is 6 hours motionless but aware.
Defy Death: advantage on death saving throws. Hard to Kill: once per long rest, when reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, drop to 1 HP instead.

Enlightened Protection: cast protection from evil and good on yourself once per long rest without material components (Wisdom). Reject the Gods: you can't gain or lose piety. At 5th level cast dispel magic once per long rest; at 11th dispel evil and good once per long rest and dispel magic at 4th level; at 17th antimagic field once per long rest and dispel magic at 5th level.
Psychic Shield: resistance to psychic damage. Sphinx's Shroud: immune to effects that sense your emotions or read your thoughts; Insight checks to read your intentions have disadvantage.

Boon Aura: allies within 5 feet have advantage on saves against being frightened or charmed while you aren't incapacitated. Companion's Protection: once per long rest, reaction when a creature you can see within 5 feet is hit by an attack roll to be hit instead.
Cloak of Stars: once per long rest, action to wrap yourself in starlight for 1 minute, giving attack rolls against you disadvantage. Nyxborn Resistance: resistance to necrotic and radiant damage.

Ears of the Oracle: speak, read and write Celestial, and a god can speak through you. Oracle's Insight: once per short or long rest add 1d10 to an ability check (after rolling, before the result). Instead of a god's piety benefits: piety 3+ augury as a ritual, 10+ divination as a ritual, 25+ commune as a ritual and can't be surprised, each once per long rest (Wisdom); 50+ +2 Intelligence or Wisdom and that maximum.
Pious Protection: once per long rest, reroll a failed save and use the new roll. Religious Study: advantage on Religion checks about your god. Starting Piety: 3 with your chosen god.
Unscarred Resilience: once per short or long rest, reaction when you take damage to reduce it by 1d12 + your Constitution modifier.

Choose a Strixhaven college; learn two of its cantrips and one 1st-level spell, castable once per long rest without a slot or with slots (Int, Wis or Cha). Lorehold: two of light, sacred flame, thaumaturgy, plus a 1st-level cleric or wizard spell. Prismari: two of fire bolt, prestidigitation, ray of frost, plus a 1st-level bard or sorcerer spell. Quandrix: two of druidcraft, guidance, mage hand, plus a 1st-level druid or wizard spell. Silverquill: two of sacred flame, thaumaturgy, vicious mockery, plus a 1st-level bard or cleric spell. Witherbloom: two of chill touch, druidcraft, spare the dying, plus a 1st-level druid or wizard spell.

Cast find familiar as a ritual, with your college's mascot as a form (spirit statue, art elemental, fractal, inkling or pest). When you Attack, forgo one attack to let it attack with its reaction. Action: swap places with it within 60 feet, once per long rest or by spending a 2nd-level or higher slot.

Learn one cleric cantrip, augury, and one 1st-level spell set by your alignment: a warlock spell if evil, a cleric spell if good, a druid spell if neutral. Cast augury and the 1st-level spell once each per long rest without a slot, or with slots. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is the spellcasting ability (chosen with this feat), and you can use a holy symbol as a focus for spells using it.

display.prerequisite: Dragonlance Campaign, Sorcerer or Wizard class or Mage of High Sorcery background
display.description: Choose a moon of Krynn. Learn one wizard cantrip and two 1st-level spells from its list. Nuitari: dissonant whispers, false life, hex, ray of sickness. Lunitari: color spray, disguise self, feather fall, longstrider. Solinari: comprehend languages, detect evil and good, protection from evil and good, shield. Cast each 1st-level spell once per long rest without a slot, or with any slots. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is the spellcasting ability (chosen with this feat).

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Initiate of High Sorcery (Nuitari) feat
display.description: Ambitious Magic: learn one 2nd-level enchantment or necromancy spell, castable once per long rest without a slot or with slots, using your Initiate of High Sorcery ability. Life Channel: when a creature you can see within 60 feet fails a save against a damaging spell you cast, spend Hit Dice equal to the spell's level, roll them, and add the total to its damage.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Initiate of High Sorcery (Lunitari) feat
display.description: Insightful Magic: learn one 2nd-level illusion or transmutation spell, castable once per long rest without a slot or with slots, using your Initiate of High Sorcery ability. Magical Balance: when you roll 9 or lower on the d20 for an attack roll or ability check, treat it as a 10; proficiency bonus times per long rest.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Initiate of High Sorcery (Solinari) feat
display.description: Protective Magic: learn one 2nd-level abjuration or divination spell, castable once per long rest without a slot or with slots, using your Initiate of High Sorcery ability. Protective Ward: when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, use your reaction and expend a spell slot to reduce the damage by d6s equal to the slot's level plus your spellcasting modifier.

display.prerequisite: Dragonlance Campaign, Fighter or Paladin class or Knight of Solamnia background
display.description: Mount Up: mounting or dismounting costs only 5 feet of movement. Precise Strike: once per turn, give a weapon attack roll against a creature advantage; on a hit add 1d8 to the damage. Proficiency bonus uses per long rest, spent only on a hit.

+1 Strength, Dexterity or Constitution (max 20). Commanding Rally: as a bonus action, an ally within 30 feet who can see or hear you can make one weapon attack with its reaction, adding 1d8 damage on a hit; proficiency bonus times per long rest. Knights of Solamnia belong to one order at a time but keep every Knight of Solamnia feat they have gained if they change orders.

+1 Constitution, Wisdom or Charisma (max 20). Bolstering Rally: as a bonus action, a creature you can see within 30 feet (you included) that can see or hear you gains temporary HP equal to 1d8 + your proficiency bonus + the modifier of the score this feat raised; proficiency bonus times per long rest. Knights of Solamnia belong to one order at a time but keep every Knight of Solamnia feat they have gained if they change orders.

+1 Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma (max 20). Demoralizing Strike: once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, it makes a Wisdom save (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + the modifier of the score this feat raised) or is frightened of you until the end of your next turn; on a success it has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. Proficiency bonus times per long rest. Knights of Solamnia belong to one order at a time but keep every Knight of Solamnia feat they have gained if they change orders.

Choose a plane type for a damage resistance and a cantrip (cast without material components; Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma chosen with this feat). Chaotic: poison, minor illusion. Evil: necrotic, chill touch. Good: radiant, sacred flame. Lawful: force, guidance. The Outlands: psychic, mage hand.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes (Lawful) feat
display.description: +1 to one ability score (max 20). Stasis Strike: once per turn when you damage a creature you can see within 60 feet, deal an extra 1d8 force and it makes a Wisdom save (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + your Scion spellcasting modifier) or is restrained until the start of your next turn. Proficiency bonus times per long rest.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes (Evil) feat
display.description: +1 to one ability score (max 20). Grasp of Avarice: once per turn when you damage a creature you can see within 60 feet, deal an extra 1d6 + proficiency bonus necrotic and regain that many HP. Proficiency bonus times per long rest.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes (Chaotic) feat
display.description: +1 to one ability score (max 20). Chaotic Flare: when you roll a 1 or 20 on an attack roll or save, roll a d4 for a flare lasting until the end of your next turn (one at a time). 1 Battle Fury: a creature you can see has advantage on attacks and disadvantage on ability checks. 2 Disruption Field: creatures starting their turn within 5 feet of you or first entering that area on a turn take 1d8 force. 3 Unbound: you can spend movement to teleport that far to an unoccupied space you can see, once. 4 Wailing Winds: creatures within 15 feet of you, you included, have disadvantage on Wisdom saves.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes (The Outlands) feat
display.description: +1 to one ability score (max 20). Crossroads Emissary: learn misty step and tongues; cast each once per long rest without a slot (tongues needs no material components), or with slots, using your Scion spellcasting ability.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes feat
display.description: Planar Adaptation: after each long rest, choose resistance to acid, cold or fire until your next long rest. Portal Cracker: as an action, concentrate on a portal within 5 feet and make a DC 20 Int (Arcana) check; on a success force it open or closed for 1 hour (its key works only with a DC 20 Int (Arcana) check as an action), on a failure take 3d8 psychic and can't try that portal again until a long rest. Portal Sense: you know the direction to the last portal you used on the same plane, and once per long rest, as an action, detect portals within 30 feet not behind total cover.

display.prerequisite: 4th level, Scion of the Outer Planes (Good) feat
display.description: +1 to one ability score (max 20). Soothe Pain: when you or a creature within 30 feet takes damage, use your reaction to reduce it by 1d10 + proficiency bonus. Proficiency bonus times per long rest.

display.prerequisite: Spellcasting feature or Rune Carver background
display.description: Learn comprehend languages; cast it once per long rest without a slot, or with any slots. Rune Magic: you know runes equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down). After each long rest, inscribe each on a nonmagical object you touch and know its 1st-level spell until your next long rest; while carrying a marked object, cast that spell with your slots, or once per long rest per rune without a slot or material components. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is the ability (chosen with this feat). Swap one rune each level. Runes: Cloud fog cloud, Death inflict wounds, Dragon chromatic orb, Enemy disguise self, Fire burning hands, Friend speak with animals, Frost armor of Agathys, Hill goodberry, Journey longstrider, King command, Mountain entangle, Stone sanctuary, Storm thunderwave.

display.prerequisite: Martial weapon proficiency or Giant Foundling background
display.description: Choose one strike. Once per turn when you hit with a melee or thrown weapon attack, add its effect (save DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Str or Con modifier); proficiency bonus uses per long rest. Cloud: +1d4 thunder, and on a failed Wis save you are invisible to the creature until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast. Fire: +1d10 fire. Frost: +1d6 cold, and on a failed Con save its speed is 0 until the start of your next turn. Hill: +1d6 of the weapon's type, and on a failed Str save it falls prone. Stone: +1d6 force, and on a failed Str save it is pushed 10 feet. Storm: +1d6 lightning, and on a failed Con save it has disadvantage on attacks until the start of your next turn.
